item.title: UDJFB condemns torture of three DT journalists in Tongi
item.description:
The Urban Development Journalists Forum Bangladesh (UDJFB) has strongly condemned the hostage-taking, torture and death threats against three journalists, including Dhaka Tribune reporter Rabiul Hasan, who were attacked while investigating drug trafficking in Tongi, Gazipur.
Rabiul Hasan is a member of the UDJFB. The other two journalists targeted in the attack were reporter Asiful Islam Rifat and photojournalist Abir Ahmed Shupto.
In a joint statement issued on Thursday, UDJFB President Matin Abdullah and General Secretary Hasan Emon condemned the incident and demanded the immediate arrest and exemplary punishment of those responsible.
According to the statement, the three journalists went to Haji Mazar slum, under Tongi West police station, on November 6 to investigate drug trafficking as part of their professional duties. They spent around one and a half hours at the location, gathering evidence and recording video footage of alleged drug transactions.
At one stage, a group of 20 to 25 armed alleged drug traders, who had been monitoring their movements through CCTV cameras, attacked the journalists.
The attackers allegedly pointed pistols at their heads, threatened to mutilate them with sharp weapons and snatched Rabiul Hasan's mobile phone before deleting all the evidence and information they had collected.
The journalists were then taken to a nearby location and held captive for around three hours. During this time, they were brutally beaten and allegedly subjected to an attempt on their lives through gunfire.
The attackers also allegedly forced the journalists to consume a sedative and recorded videos with money and drugs placed in front of them, apparently to use the footage for blackmail.
They were eventually released after being threatened with death and warned against publishing reports on the group's drug trade and other criminal activities, the statement said.
The injured journalists subsequently received medical treatment at Shaheed Ahsan Ullah Master General Hospital in Tongi.
Expressing grave concern over repeated attacks on journalists at a location it described as a haven for criminals, the forum said such acts of violence and intimidation were aimed at silencing independent and investigative journalism.
The UDJFB said attempts by organised criminal groups to suppress factual reporting and intimidate journalists through violence threatened not only press freedom but also democratic values and freedom of expression.
The forum said the local administration and law enforcement agencies could not evade responsibility for the attack on the three journalists.
It called for an immediate crackdown in Haji Mazar slum and surrounding areas to arrest the alleged masterminds and armed attackers and bring them to justice.
The forum also urged the relevant authorities to ensure adequate security for the three journalists.
The statement was signed by Latiful Islam, office secretary of the Urban Development Journalists Forum Bangladesh (UDJFB).

item.title: Rizvi: Hasina must be extradited, not welcomed with flowers
item.description:
BNP acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi on Friday said ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina will have to be brought back to Bangladesh through the existing extradition treaty with India, stressing that she must not be welcomed as if she were returning from a visit to her parents' or in-laws' home.
“Many people have been killed, and numerous cases have been filed against Sheikh Hasina. She has also been convicted and sentenced to death for crimes against humanity. Yet, discussions about bringing her back make it sound as if she had gone to her parents’ or in-laws’ home and should be welcomed with flowers,” he said.
Rizvi said Hasina would have to be brought back in accordance with the provisions of the extradition treaty between Bangladesh and India and through the ongoing judicial and legal processes.
He made the remarks while addressing a discussion organised by the Jatiyatabadi Mohila Dal at the Jatiya Press Club, marking National Revolution and Solidarity Day.
Referring to Hasina’s intention to return to Bangladesh and her reportedly application for a passport, visa and national identity card, the BNP leader said there is no scope for her to be repatriated. “Only extradition is an option for her,” he said.
Explaining the difference, he said extradition is a legal matter between two countries, while repatriation applies to someone who has left their country without facing any allegations and later wishes to return.
“If I leave my country without any allegations against me and later want to return, I can apply to my own country for a passport if I do not have one. But can the same process can apply to someone facing criminal cases, state prosecution and sentences in their own country? Such a person is subject to extradition,” Rizvi said.
Bangladesh has an extradition treaty with India, making Hasina’s return a legal matter between the two countries, he said.
The BNP leader said Hasina killed around 1,400 people, including students and rickshaw-pullers, during the July 2024 mass uprising. “Several cases are pending against her, and she has already been sentenced in some cases, including a death sentence.”
“Why is all this fanfare over her return? She must face the ongoing trials in Bangladesh and serve the sentences handed down to her,” he said.
Turning to the role of women in politics, Rizvi said women leaders and activists of the BNP had played a significant role in the struggle for democracy during the past 17 years.
He recalled how police repeatedly erected barricades to prevent their programmes and how women activists tried to break through them despite fear of arrest, enforced disappearance and harassment.
Bangladesh wants Hasina, who faces the death penalty, to be extradited from India under the existing extradition treaty, while India has said travel documents are required for people to travel.
Hasina fled to India after student-led protests had forced her from power on August 5, 2024 and had since then remained there.
In 2025, a Bangladeshi special tribunal sentenced her to death for crimes against humanity committed during the mass uprising.

item.title: Dengue claims 2 more lives, 1,255 hospitalised in 24hrs
item.description:
Two more people died of dengue and 1,255 were hospitalised across the country in the 24 hours until 8am on Friday, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The latest fatalities have raised the death toll from the mosquito-borne disease to 483 this year.
Of the newly hospitalised patients, 434 were in Dhaka Division, 267 in Chittagong, 160 in Khulna, 147 in Barisal, 89 in Rajshahi, 76 each in Mymensingh and Rangpur, and six in Sylhet.
A total of 158,883 dengue patients have been admitted to hospitals nationwide so far this year. Of them, 152,485 have recovered and returned home.
Last year, 102,861 people were infected with dengue and 413 died from the disease.

item.title: England reach Nations League quarters as Italy beat Zidane's France
item.description:
England secured their place in the Nations League quarter-finals with a 2-1 victory over Croatia on Thursday, while Zinedine Zidane suffered his first defeat as France coach as his side lost away to Italy.
Harry Kane marked his record-breaking 126th appearance for England by scoring the winning goal from the penalty spot at Wembley, taking his international tally to 92 goals.
Morgan Rogers put England ahead in the first half before a mistake by Jarell Quansah allowed Petar Sucic to equalise for Croatia on the hour mark.
England regained the lead when Ivan Smolcic wrestled Quansah to the ground at a corner, with Kane converting the resulting penalty after a VAR review.
Thomas Tuchel's side moved to 12 points from five matches in Group A3, ensuring they will go through to the quarter-finals next March.
"Good win. We wanted this win desperately and I think we deserved it," Tuchel told ITV.
"We got the job done and it was important because it was a special occasion for Harry and he scored the winner, so perfect evening."
Spain top the section on 15 points after a 2-0 win over the Czech Republic in Prague, their fifth straight victory in the competition.
Alex Baena's penalty and a late goal from Marc Pubill extended Spain's unbeaten run in competitive matches to 44 and set up a showdown with England in Madrid on Sunday, which will decide the group winners.
The Czechs remain without a point and finished with 10 men after captain Ladislav Krejci was sent off.
Italy came from behind to beat France 3-1 in Milan and hand Zidane his first defeat since taking charge of Les Bleus.
France were without Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele due to injury but Michael Olise pounced on a loose pass from Gianluigi Donnarumma to fire them ahead on 10 minutes.
Francesco Pio Esposito steered in Nicolo Cambiaghi's pass to bring Italy level before France twice hit the post through Bradley Barcola and Rayan Cherki.
Sebastiano Esposito blazed a second-half penalty wide for Italy, but Roberto Mancini's side did not rue that miss as Davide Frattesi powered home Federico Dimarco's cut-back.
Francesco Pio Esposito then doubled his tally for the night, succeeding where his older brother had failed by converting a penalty after Dayot Upamecano fouled substitute Antonio Vergara.
Zidane put the loss down to "part of the learning process".
"You mustn't change anything just because of a defeat," he said.
Italy climbed above France at the top of Group A1 on head-to-head record. Both teams have 10 points going into the final round of games, with Belgium just one point adrift.
Belgium host Italy on Sunday and France are at home to Turkey.
Zidane said Mbappe could return for the game in Bordeaux.
"I hope he'll be available on Sunday. That was the plan, that's what we want," he said.
Turkey slid to a fifth straight loss as they went down 2-1 to Belgium in Izmir.
Arda Guler's magnificent free-kick put Turkey ahead under new coach and former midfielder Sergen Yalcin, but Belgium struck twice in quick succession with goals from Kevin De Bruyne and Charles De Ketelaere to come away with victory.

item.title: Climate resilience must be accessible by design
Kerry sees US climate comeback as states and businesses defy Trump’s retreat
item.description:
Former US climate envoy John Kerry has expressed confidence that the United States will eventually return to a leading role in global climate action, arguing that the country's clean energy transition is continuing despite the Trump administration's withdrawal from international climate cooperation.
Speaking at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya on Tuesday, Kerry criticised the administration's efforts to roll back environmental protections, promote fossil fuels and undermine renewable energy.
He said the federal government's political direction did not reflect the broader momentum for clean energy across the United States.
“We will build and rebuild our partnerships,” Kerry said, expressing hope that the US would re-engage with international climate efforts in the future.
Kerry, who served as US secretary of state under former president Barack Obama and as President Joe Biden's special presidential envoy for climate, signed the Paris Agreement on behalf of the United States in 2016.
The US withdrawal from the Paris Agreement took effect on January 27, 2026, marking another retreat by the world's largest historical emitter from international climate cooperation.
However, Kerry said state and local governments, as well as private businesses, were continuing to invest in clean energy, creating jobs and generating economic benefits across political boundaries.
He noted that renewable energy and other low-carbon technologies were attracting investment in both Republican- and Democratic-led states.
Speaking to journalists on the sidelines of the summit, Kerry also urged climate advocates to change how they communicate the urgency of climate action.
“I think everybody who is working on climate needs to change the way they talk about it,” he said.
He argued that climate change should not be presented solely as an environmental or scientific issue. Instead, advocates should highlight its implications for employment, public health, national security, food supplies and community stability.
Kerry also took part in an energy transition discussion with former US vice-president Al Gore on Tuesday, highlighting the need to reduce dependence on fossil fuels and expand investment in clean energy.
He stressed that electrification alone would not guarantee emissions reductions, noting that its climate benefits would depend on how electricity was generated.
If rising electricity demand continued to be met by coal and natural gas, electrification could fail to deliver the expected emissions reductions, he cautioned.
His remarks came as United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres urged world leaders to accelerate the transition away from fossil fuels.
Addressing leaders at COP31 on Wednesday, Guterres challenged the influence of fossil fuel interests in climate policymaking.
“Fossil fuels must go the way of the dinosaurs,” he said. “The dinosaurs did not have a lobby. Fossil fuels do.”
Guterres called for a “climate justice compact” to strengthen international cooperation, mobilise climate finance and protect communities facing the worst effects of global warming.
He also proposed taxing the windfall profits of major oil companies to help finance support for countries suffering climate-related losses and damage.
The proposal reflects growing frustration among climate-vulnerable countries over the gap between international commitments and the financial support reaching communities most exposed to climate change.
For developing countries such as Bangladesh, predictable climate financing is essential to protect coastal communities, agricultural livelihoods, infrastructure and public health.
At COP28 in Dubai in 2023, countries agreed to transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems in a just, orderly and equitable manner. However, translating that commitment into national policies, investment and measurable emissions reductions remains a major challenge.
Countries continue to differ over the pace of the transition, the role of natural gas and the financial responsibilities of developed and developing economies.
Kerry's remarks at COP31 highlighted how climate leadership may extend beyond national governments to businesses, local authorities, investors and civil society. His expectation of renewed US engagement offered a note of optimism, even as negotiations continue over climate finance and stronger action to reduce emissions.

item.description:

He passed away at 10:05am on Friday.
The news of his death was confirmed by the late singer's friend Ershadul Haque Tinku.
Shaikh Shahed Ali was a familiar name in Bangladesh's band music scene in the 1990s. He had been seriously ill for some time and was receiving treatment at Azgar Ali Hospital in the capital.
Shahed was admitted to hospital on October 24 after his blood sodium levels dropped. While undergoing treatment, he suffered a mild stroke and also tested positive for dengue.
As his condition deteriorated, he was transferred to Azgar Ali Hospital via Square Hospital. The musician had also been undergoing regular dialysis for the past four years due to kidney complications.
His illness put on hold plans to release 24 new songs, which he had worked on over 11 years.
The musician had been scheduled to release four CDs, cassettes and vinyl records on November 6.
The founder of the band "Gachh" Shaikh Shahed, won over listeners with songs such as "Rokzana", "Upolobdhi," "Khola Chul" and "Prem Ashbei."

Eight Chinese students leave DU early after series of crude bomb blasts
item.description:
Eight Chinese students are leaving Dhaka University (DU) ahead of schedule following a series of crude bomb explosions on campus that raised security concerns.
Two have already returned to China, while the remaining six are scheduled to leave on Friday.
The students had come to DU to attend a special course on the Bangla language and Bangladeshi culture offered by the university's Institute of Modern Languages (IML). They were originally scheduled to complete their course and examinations and return home in late November.
Professor Dr MA Kawser, provost of Sir P J Hartog International Hall, the university's residential hall for foreign students, confirmed the matter to Dhaka Tribune on Thursday.
He said the eight students from China's Guangdong University of Foreign Studies became concerned after a series of crude bomb explosions on campus. Their families were also worried, prompting them to decide to return home early on the advice of their university.
The students were initially scheduled to return after completing their examinations in the last week of November. However, two have already left, while the remaining six have confirmed their flight tickets, Professor Kawser said.
He recalled that two of the students were passing near one of the explosion sites when a crude bomb went off. Witnessing the incident left them frightened and prompted their decision to return to China.
He added that the students would complete their remaining examinations through their university after returning to China.
Meanwhile, the hall authorities discussed campus security with other foreign students on Wednesday afternoon. They were assured that measures were being taken to strengthen security at the hall and across the university. The other students are currently monitoring the situation.
The IML offers special Bangla language courses for foreign students, providing an opportunity to learn about the language and culture of Bangladesh.
According to institute data, 15 students from two Chinese universities participated in the program in 2024, 19 from three universities in 2025 and 26 from four universities in 2026. Students from Guangdong University of Foreign Studies are among the participants.
A series of crude bomb explosions has rocked different parts of the DU campus over the past few days.
At least eight crude bombs exploded at six locations on Sunday evening.
Another explosion occurred in the TSC area on Monday.
Although no one was injured in those incidents, the explosions sparked panic across the campus.
On Tuesday, another crude bomb exploded in front of the academic building of the Faculty of Business Studies, injuring one person.
A separate explosion was also reported in the Shadow area beside the Faculty of Arts building on the same day.

item.title: Drug kingpins evade repeated raids at Feni’s Bede settlement
item.description:
Despite repeated anti-drug raids at Feni’s Lalpol Bede settlement, the alleged masterminds behind the drug trade remain at large, raising questions about the effectiveness of law enforcement operations.
In the latest raid on Wednesday, law enforcement agencies detained 14 people and seized Tk17.51 lakh in cash, a money-counting machine, 600 Yaba pills and 30 litres of locally distilled liquor, reports Bangla Tribune.
The three-hour operation, conducted from 5pm to 8pm, was led by Additional Superintendent of Police (Sadar Circle) Nishat Tabassum, with officials from the district administration and Feni Model Police Station.
Police said cases were being prepared against the detainees before they were sent to court.
Nishat said drug trading in the Lalpol settlement was widely known and police regularly conducted operations there. However, the alleged operators managed to escape by receiving advance information about the raids, she said.
She identified three people—Sohel, Tarek and Shirin—as the alleged controllers of the drug business, adding that they faced multiple cases.
The failure to apprehend the alleged ringleaders has raised concerns about whether repeated raids are disrupting the drug network or merely detaining people at the lower levels.
On plans to evict the settlement, Nishat said a committee had been formed through the district law and order committee to oversee the process. As many people live there, the eviction could not be completed in a single day, but preparations were underway to begin it soon.
She added that police operations would continue until the eviction was carried out.

item.title: PM leaves Antalya for Dhaka after attending COP31
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman left Antalya, Türkiye, for Dhaka on Thursday afternoon after attending the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) and the Antalya Leaders' Summit.
He departed Antalya Airport at 4:15pm local time by a Turkish Airlines flight for Istanbul, said PM's Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu.
Ambassador Subutay Yuksel, a high-ranking official at the Türkiye's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, saw the prime minister off at the airport.
Tarique is scheduled to leave Istanbul for Dhaka at 7:30pm local time and arrive at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at 5:50am on Friday.
The prime minister arrived in Antalya on Tuesday on a three-day official visit to attend COP31 and the Antalya Leaders' Summit.
On Thursday, he addressed the High-Level Segment of COP31, outlining five urgent actions to address the needs of climate-vulnerable countries.
On the sidelines of the conference, Tarique held bilateral meetings with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Chinese Vice-President Han Zheng and Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev.
During the meetings, they discussed ways to strengthen bilateral ties, expand trade and investment, and enhance cooperation in addressing the impacts of climate change.
The prime minister also held courtesy meetings and exchanged greetings with several other world leaders and heads of international organisations during the conference.
Tarique and his wife Dr Zubaida Rahman attended a dinner hosted by Turkish President Erdoğan and First Lady Emine Erdoğan in honour of world leaders attending COP31.
Apart from participating in various programmes of the conference, he visited the Bangladesh Pavilion and an exhibition of environment-friendly jute products set up in the Green Zone.

item.title: Bicycles ease girls’ access to education in Panchagarh
item.description:
A group of teenage girls ride their bicycles in a line along rural roads, passing green paddy fields on their way to school, college or madrasa. Some wear white hijabs, while others sport colourful scarves, all dressed in blue uniforms.
The sight has become increasingly common in the remote villages of Atwari upazila in Panchagarh.
Until a few years ago, many girls in the area had to walk long distances to reach their educational institutions. The time and effort involved, coupled with limited transport options, often made it difficult for them to continue their studies. Bicycles are now helping change that situation.
With support from their families, many girls are learning to ride bicycles from an early age. By their teenage years, cycling has become an essential part of their daily lives.
Every morning and afternoon, groups of girls can be seen cycling along village roads. Besides travelling to school, they use their bicycles to attend private tuition, visit classmates and meet other daily needs.
Samsun Nahar, a Class X student at Dangirhat Adarsha High School, said cycling had made her journey to school much easier.
“Earlier, I had to walk a long way to school. It took a lot of time and left me tired before classes began. Now I can reach school much faster by bicycle. Riding with friends is enjoyable and makes me feel safer,” she said.
Saving time and gaining greater freedom of movement are among the main benefits of cycling. Journeys that once required lengthy walks can now be completed much faster, making it easier for girls to attend educational institutions farther from home.
Cycling in groups also gives girls a greater sense of security and confidence. Travelling together helps them feel less vulnerable to uncomfortable situations and potential harassment along the way.
Imdadul Haque, a parent from Sardarpara village, said distance and safety had previously been major concerns for families.
“We used to worry about how our daughters would get to school, particularly because of the distance. Now they ride together in groups. It saves time and has eased some of our concerns. Most importantly, they can continue their education,” he said.
Riding along village roads, from unpaved stretches to highways, is also helping girls develop mobility skills, confidence and a sense of independence.
The change has been driven largely by growing awareness and support among families. Many parents now encourage their daughters to learn to ride bicycles from an early age to help them continue their education. For families living far from schools and colleges, bicycles have become a practical and affordable means of transport.
Sharmin Parvin, headteacher of Atwari Government Pilot Girls' High School, said transportation played an important role in ensuring students' regular attendance.
“Travelling to educational institutions can be difficult for girls from remote areas, particularly when they have to cover long distances. Bicycles have eased that problem considerably. They are also helping girls become more confident and independent,” she said.
The benefits of cycling extend beyond making daily journeys to educational institutions easier. Improved access to schools and colleges can remove one of the practical barriers that often disrupt girls' education.
It can also contribute to efforts to prevent child marriage by helping girls stay in education, broaden their future opportunities and develop greater independence.
Jahidul Islam, acting upazila secondary education officer in Atwari, said access to transportation was important for expanding girls' education in rural areas.
“Bicycles are enabling many students from remote villages to travel to educational institutions more easily. This can help ensure regular attendance, maintain continuity in education and build confidence and independence among girls. Families and communities should encourage such initiatives,” he said.
The sight of girls cycling through Atwari represents more than just a convenient way of getting to school. It reflects changing family attitudes, progress in rural girls' education and the growing independence of young women.
As they pedal past green fields and along village roads, the girls of Panchagarh are moving towards a future where distance no longer has to stand in the way of education.

item.title: Two phones seized as SP accused of information leak
item.description:
A superintendent of police (SP) serving at the Chittagong Range Reserve Force (RRF) has been placed under surveillance over allegations of sharing sensitive police information with the activities-banned Awami League.
Police have seized SP Mohammad Jahangir Alam's personal and official mobile phones as part of an investigation into the allegations, said Chittagong Range Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Abdul Quddus Chowdhury.
He said Jahangir was called in to explain certain administrative matters before his two phones were seized. An investigation committee, headed by Additional DIG (Operations) Shafizul Islam, has been formed to examine the allegations.
The DIG said Jahangir had not been arrested, dismissing reports of his detention that had circulated among police personnel.
Additional DIG Shafizul Islam said Jahangir was summoned on Tuesday, but the meeting should not be described as an interrogation or detention.
The seized phones have been sent to the Special Branch in Dhaka for forensic examination. If the allegations are substantiated, the committee will submit a report to police headquarters, which will decide on further action, he added.
Sources at the Chittagong Range office said Jahangir, a 28th batch Bangladesh Civil Service (Police) officer, was accused of supplying internal and sensitive police information to the Awami League. They claimed preliminary evidence of information leaks had been found.
A senior police official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said information about Jahangir's alleged links with the activities-banned party had prompted senior officials to summon him. He was later released and is currently performing his duties, although he remains under surveillance.
Jahangir joined the police force on December 1, 2010, and is currently serving as deputy commandant of the RRF in Chittagong.
During the anti-discrimination student movement, he was posted as additional superintendent of police in Feni. He had also faced allegations of maintaining contact with leaders and activists of the activities-banned organisation during that period.

item.title: 10 police, 18 militants killed in Pakistan’s northwest
item.description:
Gunmen attacked police during an operation against illegal gold mining in northwestern Pakistan on Wednesday, killing 10 officers, while 18 militants died in the ensuing fighting, an official police statement said.
A statement by provincial police in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa said officers were returning from a mine in the Gumbat area of Kohat district when militants opened fire on them.
In addition to the 10 police and 18 militant deaths, 12 police personnel were wounded, the statement said.
In the aftermath of the clashes, the Pakistani Taliban, the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), claimed responsibility for a series of attacks across the country, including one on a police convoy in the Gumbat area.
Earlier, a senior administrative official in Kohat told AFP that militants set two police vehicles on fire during the assault, while two other police vehicles and one private vehicle were missing.
Another senior administrative official in the Orakzai area of Kohat said that 10 militants belonging to the TTP were killed during a separate operation in the district.
A large quantity of weapons was also recovered from the militants, the official added.
Security forces are battling an intensifying militancy in the border province they say emanates from Afghanistan, an accusation its Taliban government denies.
A spokesman for a local emergency service earlier on Wednesday said there had been a “firing incident involving police personnel” in Kohat district, adding that rescue workers were treating a dozen wounded officers.
Relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan have been fraught since the Taliban authorities took power in 2021, and worsened after deadly border clashes in October last year that led to near-total closure of the border.
Clashes subsided after mediation, but the conflict intensified again in February, with Pakistan declaring “an open war” on its neighbor.
In a statement, Pakistan’s President Asif Ali Zardari condemned the attack, expressed his sorrow over the deaths of the police and said “national determination to completely eradicate terrorism from the country is unwavering.”
Pakistan’s foreign minister Ishaq Dar said he was “deeply grieved by the loss of precious lives in a cowardly terrorist attack on our police personnel in Kohat.”
Islamabad accuses Kabul of allowing militants responsible for deadly attacks on Pakistani territory to operate from its soil. Afghanistan’s Taliban authorities have denied the allegations.
Hundreds of civilians have been killed in fighting between the two countries since October last year, according to figures from the United Nations’ mission in Afghanistan.
Earlier this month, militants in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa killed two police officers assigned to protect a polio vaccination team travelling near the Afghan border.
The province was placed under emergency rule last month in a move authorities said came in reaction to the failure by the provincial government to act against militancy.
The imposition of emergency measures sidelined the last remaining bastion of power for jailed former prime minister Imran Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party.
The special constitutional measures also set off a province-wide crackdown on Khan’s supporters, with hundreds of detentions.

item.title: Two garment factories in Gazipur shut indefinitely amid labour unrest
item.description:
Authorities have indefinitely shut down two garment factories in Gazipur following allegations that workers refused to work despite reporting to their workplaces and vandalized factory premises amid demands for a minimum wage hike.
Workers arriving at the factories on Thursday morning found notices at the main gates announcing the closures.
The factories are MM Knitwear Ltd and Mamun Knitwear Ltd, both located in Konabari.
The management of both factories announced the closures effective Thursday.
According to a notice signed by the deputy manager of the administration and human resources department of MM Knitwear Ltd, workers stopped working after the lunch break on Tuesday (November 10), demanding an increase in the minimum wage.
Despite repeated requests, the workers remained inside the factory but refused to work without any reasonable cause, the notice said. It added that they later brought workers down from different production floors, vandalised factory property and left the premises.
The notice further stated that workers resumed their work stoppage on Wednesday morning, creating disorder inside the factory through intimidation and physical altercations.
Describing the workers' actions as an illegal strike, the notice said the management was compelled to suspend operations indefinitely from Thursday to protect factory property and ensure the safety of lives and assets amid continued labour unrest.
The closure was announced under Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006. The notice said the date for resuming operations would be communicated once conditions became favourable.
Attempts to contact officials at the two factories for comment were unsuccessful.
Gazipur Industrial Police Superintendent Mohammad Amzad Hossain said the factory authorities had declared an indefinite closure. Police have been deployed to maintain normalcy in the area.

item.title: Factory workers block Dhaka-Tangail Highway again demanding higher wages

Humaiun: World leaders see Tarique as ‘transformative leader’
item.description:
World leaders are viewing Prime Minister Tarique Rahman as a “transformative leader” following Bangladesh’s democratic transition, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said on Wednesday.
“They are describing him as a transformative leader during courtesy meetings and bilateral talks,” he told a press conference at the Bangladesh Pavilion on the sidelines of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkiye.
Humaiun Kobir said leaders were taking note of Tarique’s democratic mandate and his role in leading a country with a population of around 180 to 200 million people.
The prime minister attended the opening and plenary sessions of the World Leaders’ Summit on Wednesday and held courtesy meetings with the presidents of Brazil, the Maldives, Iran, Syria and Somalia, the prime ministers of Moldova, Pakistan and Kuwait, the Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), the Mayor of London and the president of the Global Zero Waste Foundation.
He also held bilateral meetings with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Chinese Vice-President Han Zheng.
Humaiun Kobir said the meetings were held in a cordial atmosphere, with the leaders congratulating Tarique on Bangladesh’s democratic transition and his electoral mandate.
They also expressed interest in strengthening bilateral ties and working with Bangladesh on issues of international importance, he said.
During his meeting with the Brazilian President, Prime Minister Tarique invited him to visit Bangladesh, and the invitation was accepted, the state minister said. The Maldivian President also expressed interest in visiting Bangladesh soon.
The Syrian President sought Bangladesh’s cooperation in rebuilding his country, particularly in development, investment, skilled manpower and employment generation, he said.
Humaiun Kobir said talks with the Pakistani Prime Minister covered regional stability, the situation in the Middle East and other issues of mutual interest.
During his meeting with the OIC Secretary General, Tarique reaffirmed Bangladesh’s firm position on Palestine and its continued support for a two-state solution, he said.
The Mayor of London had expressed interest in meeting Tarique, who had lived in London for many years, and they held a courtesy meeting, the state minister said.
He said the meeting with the Kuwaiti Prime Minister focused on the long-standing friendly relations between the two countries and ways to expand investment and economic partnership.
At his bilateral meeting with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, Tarique discussed establishing direct air connectivity between Dhaka and Tashkent, simplifying visa procedures and expanding bilateral relations.
Humaiun Kobir said the Uzbek President invited the Prime Minister to visit Uzbekistan, and Tarique assured him that he would consider visiting around the New Year.
At the meeting with Chinese Vice-President Han Zheng, the two sides discussed strengthening political and economic relations with China, one of Bangladesh’s key development partners, he said.
The state minister said the talks focused particularly on increasing Chinese investment in energy, heavy industries, infrastructure and employment-generating sectors.
He said the possibility of Chinese investment in potential energy projects, including floating storage regasification units (FSRUs), was also discussed.
The two sides also exchanged views on the possibility of developing a regional economic corridor linking Bangladesh, China and Myanmar, and on China's support for resolving the Rohingya crisis.
Bangladesh expects China's cooperation in finding a lasting solution to the crisis, which, Humaiun Kobir said, would require bilateral and multilateral initiatives as well as coordinated international efforts.
Referring to Tarique’s meeting with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan on Tuesday, the state minister described it as highly fruitful, saying the two leaders discussed political relations, mutual cooperation and various international issues.
They also discussed the possibility of Bangladesh playing a role in promoting peace in the Muslim world, he said.
Humaiun Kobir said Bangladesh had extensive experience in UN peacekeeping operations and would positively consider opportunities to contribute to peace efforts in the Muslim world, taking its national interests into account.
Meanwhile, Tarique’s wife, Dr Zubaida Rahman, attended a COP31 side event on zero-waste management. She highlighted the government’s policy initiatives to turn waste into resources and energy, as well as the need for technological cooperation in this area.
The state minister said Tarique would present Bangladesh’s position and priorities for addressing the impacts of climate change at the World Leaders’ Summit on Thursday. He is also scheduled to attend several other important programmes and meetings.
Prime Minister’s Press Secretary Saleh Shibly and Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu were present at the press conference.

Two dead, several injured after New York building collapses
item.description:
Two people were killed Wednesday and at least 17 others injured, including children, after a three-story building collapsed near a construction site in New York, city authorities said.
Images from the scene showed firefighters sifting through a pile of rubble in front of what appeared to be a residential property with its walls torn down, exposing a bedroom and a clothing wardrobe.
The building fell into a neighboring excavation site, trapping several people who firefighters worked to free over several hours using drones, search dogs and chainsaws.
"We do not know how many people are still in the collapse zone, and this will be a prolonged operation," FDNY Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore told reporters at the scene in Flatbush, Brooklyn, late Wednesday.
She said two people had died, without disclosing their ages, and said 17 others were hurt, including seven children. Four people were critically injured.
More than 250 firefighters and paramedics responded to the scene, the FDNY wrote on X, adding that the cause of the collapse was under investigation.
New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani praised the emergency services for their work, saying the site involved "precarious wreckage to navigate and dangerous voids beneath the surface."
"I want to ask New Yorkers to please take a moment to pray for those who passed away today and all of those who are mourning their loss," he added at a news conference.
One witness, named only as Anthony, told PIX11 News that he heard people screaming and a "bomb"-like noise as the building collapsed.
Another witness, Melissa Orna, told The New York Times: "The whole building started shaking, and then it just fell."
The city's Department of Buildings said its inspectors were on the scene "assisting with recovery operations and conducting structural stability inspections of nearby buildings."
Ahmed Tigani, commissioner of the department, said construction workers were performing excavation at the time of the collapse.
He added that developers had plans approved for a three-story building at the site and were pursuing permission for a nine-story building.

item.title: Dhaka ranks 9th among world's most polluted cities
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 9th among the world's most polluted cities on Thursday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 145 at 10:30am.
According to the AQI scale, the city's air quality was classified as 'unhealthy for sensitive groups,' posing minor health risks to vulnerable people.
Pakistan's Lahore topped the list with an AQI score of 363, followed by India's Delhi at 269 and China’s Beijing at 174.
According to the AQI scale, readings of 101-150 are considered unhealthy for sensitive groups, while scores of 151-200 indicate unhealthy air quality. Readings of 201-300 are classified as very unhealthy, and scores above 301 are considered hazardous, posing serious health risks.
The AQI measures daily air quality and indicates pollution levels and their potential effects on public health.
In Bangladesh, air quality is assessed based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulphur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths worldwide each year, primarily from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.description:
A life-term prisoner at Kashimpur High-Security Central Jail in Gazipur was taken to hospital after suffering severe abdominal pain, with doctors later recovering more than 50 gas lighters, nail clippers, screws and brick fragments from his stomach.
The prisoner, Hasmat Ali, 44, underwent surgery at Dhaka Medical College Hospital on November 4 after doctors diagnosed him with a condition described as “acute abdomen with an epigastric mass”.
Hasmat is the son of the late Chamed Ali Chamer of Ramdebpur village in Ghatail upazila of Tangail. He is serving a life sentence in connection with a criminal case.
Abdullah Al Mamun, senior jail superintendent of Kashimpur High-Security Central Jail, said Hasmat complained of abdominal pain at around 7:30pm on October 31.
He was initially transferred to Dhaka Central Jail in Keraniganj before being admitted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for treatment.
Mamun said Hasmat had been emotionally distressed following his father's murder. While in prison, he expressed interest in engaging in various activities to cope with his mental distress.
The prison authorities subsequently assigned him cleaning duties. While working, Hasmat allegedly collected discarded gas lighters from rubbish and swallowed them.
He eventually fell ill and was taken to hospital, where medical examinations revealed the objects in his stomach, prompting doctors to perform surgery.
Mamun said Hasmat was currently in stable condition and receiving treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital under the custody of Dhaka Central Jail authorities.

item.title: US withdraws from U17 World Cup in Qatar over security fears
item.description:
The United States withdrew Wednesday from the upcoming Under-17 soccer World Cup in Qatar due to concerns about security in the Middle East.
Players were informed of the decision just over a week before the tournament is due to begin on November 19, in a letter sent by the sport's US governing body.
"We are writing to inform you of the difficult decision to cancel our World Cup pre-camp and our planned participation in the World Cup," said the letter, seen by AFP.
"We are extremely proud of the preparation by our players and coaches to represent the US in the World Cup.
"Unfortunately, in light of current circumstances including the US State Department's Level 3 Travel Advisory for Qatar and related directives for Embassy staff and families, we are no longer able to participate in the tournament.
"The well-being of our players and staff will always be our top priority."
The war in the Middle East began in February with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which retaliated by targeting, among others, Gulf countries allied with Washington.
Diplomatic efforts to end the conflict have been punctuated by repeated threats from the United States and Israel to resume bombardments of Iran.
Multiple sporting events in the Middle East have been affected, including the tennis WTA Finals which were scheduled to be held in Saudi Arabia -- which neighbors Qatar -- but are instead now taking place at Indian Wells in the US.
This season's Formula One Grand Prix in Jeddah was cancelled, while the race in Bahrain was called off and later rescheduled under the same name in Malaysia.
Several events in Saudi Arabia have also been cancelled or postponed in recent weeks following attacks on the country by the Houthis in Yemen.
The US was one of 48 teams scheduled to play in the Under-17 World Cup, in a group with Montenegro, Chile and Algeria.
The Under-17 World Cup shifted to an annual event last year, and is being held in Qatar for five consecutive years.
Announcing its host decision in 2024, FIFA said the decision to choose a single host nation for multiple editions centered on the ability to make "use of existing footballing infrastructure in the interest of tournament efficiencies and sustainability".
Qatar was the venue for the 2022 men's World Cup.

item.title: TIB condemns state minister's remarks on gifts to engineers, demands withdrawal
item.description:
Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) has strongly condemned remarks by the state minister for local government, rural development and cooperatives, saying they appear to legitimise bribery under the guise of gifts.
At the inauguration of a training program for newly appointed assistant engineers of the Local Government Engineering Department (LGED) on Tuesday, the state minister reportedly said gifts offered to engineers from contractors' profits after bills are paid promptly, provided work quality is maintained, do not constitute bribes and may be accepted.
TIB questioned whether the remarks effectively legitimise bribery by suggesting that government engineers can receive personal benefits from contractors in return for performing their official duties.
The organisation demanded the immediate withdrawal of the remarks, clarification of the government's position and accountability for both the state minister and the secretary whose advice was reportedly cited in support of the statement.
TIB Executive Director Dr Iftekharuzzaman said verifying work quality, accepting completed projects and ensuring prompt payment of bills in accordance with regulations are routine responsibilities of government engineers.
"Engineers receive salaries and benefits from public funds precisely to perform these duties. Why, then, should they accept illicit payments from contractors under the guise of 'gifts' in return for carrying out their responsibilities?" he said.
He questioned whether the state minister was effectively encouraging the acceptance of bribes by suggesting that engineers could receive gifts for performing their official duties.
Advising newly appointed engineers, whose responsibility is to prevent irregularities in public procurement, to earn money outside the rules from contractors at the outset of their careers was irresponsible and unlawful, he said.
If such remarks are accepted, they could legitimise demands for bribes at the field level and lead to a wider spread of corruption, Iftekharuzzaman added.
He also urged the state minister to identify publicly the law or regulation that permits engineers to receive personal benefits from contractors' profits in exchange for performing their routine duties.
Citing relevant legal provisions, the TIB executive director said Section 161 of the Penal Code makes accepting gratification beyond legally authorised remuneration for performing official duties punishable by law. Section 165 also provides for punishment for accepting valuable items from individuals connected to an official's duties.
He further referred to Rule 5(1) of the Government Servants (Conduct) Rules, 1979, which requires prior government approval, subject to specified exceptions, for accepting gifts that create an obligation towards the donor.
Rule 5(4) sets a Tk500 limit for each gift received by secretaries and officers of equivalent rank from specified sources, while Paragraph 6(2) of Schedule 20 of the Public Procurement Rules, 2025 allows certain low-value promotional items, such as diaries, calendars and pens bearing an organisation's logo, worth up to Tk5,000 per item.
However, neither provision allows engineers to receive personal benefits from contractors as a reward for performing their official duties, he said.
Highlighting the risk of conflicts of interest, Iftekharuzzaman said engineers who accept personal benefits from contractors whose work they supervise may compromise their impartiality.
Such transactions could influence project supervision and bill certification, undermine fair competition among contractors and encourage collusion between engineers and contractors, he added.
He warned that the practice could spread to other government departments, normalising illicit payments under the guise of gifts as a condition for receiving public services.
The TIB executive director also questioned the state minister's reference to advice from a senior secretary.
"If the senior secretary did indeed offer such advice, as described by the state minister, serious questions arise about the secretary's professional integrity and ethical fitness to remain in office," he said.
He also questioned whether there was an attempt to institutionalise collusive corruption between the state minister and the senior secretary, adding that such a position would be embarrassing for the government and the ruling party and contradict the government's election manifesto.
Referring to a previous controversy over the road transport and bridges minister's remarks describing extortion as a matter of negotiated transactions, Iftekharuzzaman said corruption-enabling statements by senior government officials should be treated as warning signs.
TIB called on the state minister to publicly apologise and unconditionally withdraw his remarks. It also urged the government to seek a formal explanation from him, ensure accountability and verify the authenticity of the senior secretary's alleged advice before taking appropriate legal action.

item.title: COP31 pledge targets $156b annual investment to boost electrification
item.description:
Governments, energy agencies and businesses have pledged to accelerate global electrification, with an annual investment commitment of $156 billion for power grids, renewable energy and storage announced at the COP31 climate summit on Tuesday.
The COP31 35-by-35 Global Electrification Pledge aims to raise electricity’s share of global final energy consumption from around 23% to at least 35% by 2035, accelerating the shift to electric transport, buildings and industries. It has received backing from 180 companies with combined annual revenues of $1.69 trillion.
COP31 President Murat Kurum said electrification was essential to strengthen energy security, reduce emissions and support economic growth, particularly amid growing concerns over dependence on imported energy.
The Utilities for Net Zero Alliance (UNEZA) raised its annual investment commitment from $148 billion to $156 billion. The International Energy Agency (IEA) will track progress through a global monitoring mechanism, while the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) will help developing countries identify investment needs and access financing.
The COP31 presidency is also establishing an Electrify Now Finance Coalition, bringing together governments, development banks and private financial institutions to mobilise funding for emerging and developing economies. The World Bank and African Development Bank are set to serve as its inaugural co-chairs in 2027.
However, campaigners have questioned whether rising electricity demand will be met with renewable energy or additional fossil fuel generation.
Claire Smith of the civil society coalition Beyond Fossil Fuels warned that electrification could increase fossil fuel consumption unless accompanied by renewable energy expansion, stronger grids and storage facilities. The pledge does not explicitly require all additional electricity to come from clean sources, leaving countries to determine their own energy mix.
Türkiye's continued investment in oil and gas has also raised questions about the consistency of its climate ambitions. President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan recently announced two new oil fields with an estimated combined potential of 135 million barrels, while reporting daily production of 84,000 barrels in the Gabar region.
Climate Action Tracker rates Türkiye's overall climate action as “critically insufficient”, citing continued investment in fossil fuels despite progress in wind and solar energy.
The debate has particular significance for developing countries such as Bangladesh, where dependence on imported fossil fuels, limited access to affordable finance and inadequate infrastructure remain major challenges. Expanding renewable energy, upgrading distribution networks and securing technology and investment will be crucial to a sustainable transition.
Further discussions on climate finance are scheduled for November 13. The broader challenge for COP31 will be to turn investment pledges into measurable action and ensure that electrification delivers affordable, reliable and cleaner energy without deepening debt or prolonging fossil fuel dependence.

item.title: Dengue: 4 more die, 1,900 hospitalized in 24hrs
item.description:
Four dengue patients died in the last 24 hours till 8am on Wednesday, while 1,900 were hospitalized after being infected with the mosquito-borne disease during the same period.
The latest fatalities have raised the country's dengue death toll to 478 this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the newly-hospitalized dengue patients, 780 were in Dhaka Division, 85 in Mymensingh Division, 242 in Chittagong Division, 226 in Khulna Division, 198 in Rajshahi Division, 109 in Rangpur Division, 249 in Barisal Division and 11 in Sylhet Division.
According to the report, a total of 155,668 dengue patients have, so far, been hospitalized across the country this year.
So far, 149,123 dengue patients have recovered and returned home after receiving treatment in the hospitals.
A total of 102,861 people were infected with dengue, and 413 people died from the mosquito-borne disease last year.

item.title: Home minister: 316 killed in armed group attacks in CHT over five years
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has said that 316 people were killed in attacks by armed groups in the Chittagong Hill Tracts (CHT) over the past 5 years, including 308 civilians and 8 members of the security forces.
During the same period, 435 civilians and 55 members of the security forces were injured.
The home minister provided the information on behalf of the prime minister in response to a written question from SA Jinnah Kabir, member of parliament for Manikganj-1, during the question-and-answer session on the third day of the fourth session of the National Parliament on Wednesday.
In his question, SA Jinnah Kabir sought information on attacks, abductions, forcible extortion and the use of illegal firearms by armed groups, as well as attacks on members of the army and other law enforcement agencies.
He also asked about incidents affecting the security of Bengalis and people from different small ethnic groups living in the CHT districts of Rangamati, Khagrachhari and Bandarban over the past 5 years, including the number of people killed and injured.
In response, Salahuddin Ahmed said armed groups had carried out 97 attacks on security forces over the past 5 years. During this period, 194 attacks targeted the Bengali community and 81 targeted small ethnic groups.
In addition, 297 people were abducted, forcible extortion was carried out in 471 incidents, and illegal firearms were used in 377 incidents.
Outlining the government's measures to control the security situation in the hill districts, the home minister said the special armed forces operation, "Operation Uttaran", was ongoing to maintain peace and order and suppress terrorist activities.
He said the Bangladesh Army, Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), police and SRB had increased regular patrols and intelligence activities to prevent terrorist activities.
A strict policy had also been adopted against illegal arms holders, extortionists and terrorists in the hills, he said. Cases were being filed under existing laws over specific allegations of crimes, and the accused were being brought under the law.
The home minister further said regular special joint operations were being conducted by the army, BGB, police and SRB to eliminate the activities of new and old regional armed groups in the CHT and recover illegal firearms.
Based on intelligence information, operations were also being conducted to destroy secret hideouts and training camps of terrorists in remote hilly areas. Helicopters were being used with assistance from the air force when required.
He said the sources and economic sectors linked to terrorists' forcible extortion were being identified and monitored.
To prevent extortion, the number of checkpoints had been increased, while intelligence surveillance of financial transactions, including mobile banking, had been strengthened.
Mentioning that the BGB's capabilities had been increased to prevent the smuggling of illegal firearms and drugs across the border, the minister said surveillance had been intensified in remote areas adjacent to the Mizoram border in India and the Myanmar border.
Police and SRB were also uncovering various sources and networks in the plains involved in supplying weapons and military uniforms, he added.
The home minister further said hundreds of active members of various regional armed groups had been arrested through continuous and special joint operations in the hills.
During these operations, advanced firearms, live ammunition, magazines, combat uniforms, drones and signal equipment used by the groups had been recovered.

item.title: COP31: Bangladesh seeks easier climate funding, renewable investment
item.description:
Bangladesh is pressing for increased funding to address climate-induced loss and damage, implement adaptation programmes and expand renewable energy at COP31 in Türkiye's Antalya, while raising concerns over the gap between international commitments and their actual implementation.
It is particularly emphasising effective financing to protect the lives and livelihoods of people in coastal areas, haors, chars and drought-prone regions.
Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo said climate change was causing economic losses of around $15.2 billion annually in Bangladesh.
He said Bangladesh would highlight its position at the conference and push for greater access to international climate funds for countries facing severe climate risks.
The country’s central demand is that climate finance should not add to its debt burden, but instead come through adequate, predictable and easily accessible grants, he said.
For countries like Bangladesh, the effectiveness of a climate conference cannot be measured by declarations and financial pledges alone.
The real test is how much of the promised support reaches vulnerable communities and translates into tangible protection on the ground.
Climate change expert Prof Dr Ainun Nishat believes implementation should be the main focus of this year’s conference, as considerable gaps remain despite political commitments and procedural decisions taken at previous climate summits.
He said establishing funds and financing mechanisms was not enough and effectiveness was needed to be assessed through proper monitoring and evaluation to determine whether the money was being used as intended.
With rising temperatures, natural disasters and climate-related risks expected to intensify, Nishat said climate considerations must be integrated into all development activities rather than being treated as a separate issue.
Bangladeshi climate scientist Dr Atiq Rahman said every country participating in the COP process was a party to the negotiations, and Bangladesh had played an important role in the past as a leading voice of the Least Developed Countries (LDCs).
Although Bangladesh is now in the process of graduating from the LDC category, its experience and role as a former leader and spokesperson of the group remain important in international climate negotiations, he said.
Rahman stressed that attention should not be limited to the decisions reached at the negotiating table; countries must also monitor what changes those decisions bring during implementation.
The growing dependence on loans in Bangladesh’s climate financing has been highlighted in a study by Change Initiative, which raises questions about the sustainability of the country’s transition to renewable energy.
Mofazzal Hossain, research coordinator at the organisation, said loans accounted for 90.4 percent of total investment in Bangladesh’s renewable energy sector since 2000.
According to the research, Bangladesh received a total of $2.54 billion in climate finance for its energy sector. Of this amount, $880 million went to coal- and gas-based power plants, including those at Matarbari and Bheramara.
The study also warns that if the existing financing pattern continues, per capita debt in the renewable energy sector could reach $105 by 2040. Bangladesh’s current per capita climate debt across all sectors stands at around $80.
The organisation has proposed establishing a national financing mechanism titled the ‘Renewable Energy Sovereignty Facility’ to reduce dependence on new public borrowing and expand investment in clean energy.
According to the organisation, the facility could mobilise $7.69 billion in investment in the renewable energy sector between 2026 and 2030.
It could also reduce new government borrowing from $4.6 billion to $800 million.
As a result, per capita debt in the renewable energy sector could fall from $105 to $24 by 2040, representing a reduction of around 77%, the organisation said.
Bangladesh is making grant-based climate finance a central demand at COP31, arguing that vulnerable countries should not have to take on additional debt to address a crisis they have contributed relatively little to creating.
Saimum Parvez, special assistant to the Prime Minister on Environment, Forest and Climate Change, said Bangladesh would strongly raise the need for adequate grant-based financing at the conference.
“Our demand is to increase grants for adaptation and addressing climate-induced losses and damage without adding to the debt burden, and to simplify the application and approval processes for climate funds,” he said.
He said the Bangladesh delegation would coordinate its position with the LDC group, the G77 and other like-minded climate-vulnerable countries to protect the country’s interests.
Several meetings had already been held to coordinate the country’s position, while the Prime Minister would also outline Bangladesh’s priorities in his address, he said.
Bangladeshi experts are also raising various climate-related issues at the conference, Parvez added.
Bangladesh has placed several issues at the centre of its negotiating agenda, with particular emphasis on securing financing without creating further debt.
These include implementing adaptation programmes and the National Adaptation Plan (NAP), securing funds to address climate-induced losses and damage, and making access to the Green Climate Fund easier.
The country is also seeking greater investment in renewable energy, a just transition away from fossil fuels, technology transfer and capacity building.
Other priorities include early warning systems and climate-resilient infrastructure in coastal areas, as well as financial support for non-economic losses such as displacement, loss of livelihoods and damage to cultural heritage.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,295 as six die in 24 hours
item.description:
Six more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Wednesday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,295.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all six of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,190, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 105, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the six new suspected fatalities, the highest concentrations were recorded in the Dhaka and Mymensingh divisions, with two deaths each.
A total of 1,351 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Wednesday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 242,907.
During the same period, 113 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 24,723.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 216,806 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 207,903 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Two buses torched in Pallabi
item.description:
Two parked passenger buses belonging to Bikalpa Paribahan and Abhijat Paribahan were set on fire by miscreants in the capital's Pallabi area on Wednesday morning.
The fire damaged the seats, windows and body of one bus, while the rear windowpanes, seats and covers of the other bus were also damaged. No casualties were reported.
The incident took place around Wednesday morning at Phulkali intersection in Section 12 under Pallabi police station.
Police said miscreants arrived on a motorcycle, set fire to the two buses parked on the roadside and fled the scene.
Local residents spotted the flames and managed to bring the fire under control by pouring water on the vehicles.
According to police, the damage to the Bikalpa Paribahan bus is estimated at Tk8 lakh to Tk10 lakh. The damage to the Abhijat Paribahan bus is estimated at around Tk50,000.
Pallabi Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Jalal Uddin said efforts are underway to identify and arrest those involved in the incident.

item.title: Al-Arafah Islami Bank holds leadership development training
item.description:
A daylong training program titled “Connect, Influence & Grow: Leadership Development & Interpersonal Excellence” was held at Al-Arafah Islami Bank Training Institute (AIBTI), aiming to enhance the leadership qualities, interpersonal skills and professional excellence of the Bank’s Senior Executives and Managers.
The program was inaugurated on November 10, Tuesday, by the bank’s managing director Mohd Rafat Ullah Khan, who attended as chief guest.
The session was chaired by principal of AIBTI Md Abdur Rahim Duary.
Mohd Rafat Ullah Khan emphasized that effective leadership, efficient communication, mutual collaboration and accountability are essential for achieving institutional goals in an evolving banking environment.
Alongside professional knowledge, he highlighted the importance of developing leadership qualities, team coordination and the ability to make positive decisions.
He expressed his optimism that such training programs would play a significant role in enhancing both the individual and institutional performance of the Bank’s officials.
The training program was facilitated by Khandaker Zia Hasan, founder and chief executive officer of Zia’s Language Centre, Canada, who attended as resource person.
Through practical discussions and experience-sharing sessions, he presented various strategies for developing leadership skills.
A total of 40 Senior Executives and Managers of the Bank participated in the training program.
The day-long session covered various aspects of leadership concepts and development, emotional intelligence, communication skills, interpersonal relationship building, fostering mutual trust and enhancing team effectiveness.
These competencies are expected to contribute to improved workplace performance and enhanced customer service.

item.title: Trends Bird, East West Chemicals sign strategic MoU
item.description:
Trends Bird Limited (TBL) and East West Chemicals Limited (EWCL) have recently signed a significant Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), marking the beginning of a strategic collaboration aimed at developing and implementing a customized Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system for EWCL.
Under the collaboration, Trends Bird Limited will design, develop, implement, deploy and hand over a customized Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system for East West Chemicals Limited.
The system is intended to bring EWCL's major operational, commercial, financial and management processes together on one platform, replacing separate working methods with a connected, data-driven approach.
The ERP will cover key areas of EWCL's business, including procurement and inventory, import and LC management, quality control, batch and expiry management, depot and distribution management, sales, delivery and collection, finance and accounts, audit and management controls, and HR and field force functions.
The collaboration reflects a shared vision of strengthening EWCL's digital capability and building a lasting working relationship between the two companies.

item.title: Act early, Live life Shukhee
item.description:
Millions of people in Bangladesh live with diabetes without knowing it, and many discover it only when complications have already reached their eyes, kidneys, heart or feet. Yet with early screening, timely care and simple changes in daily life, diabetes can be prevented, delayed and managed well. To mark World Diabetes Day under the global theme "Early action on diabetes", Grameen HealthTech Limited (Shukhee), in partnership with Experto ReWell, hosted a seminar titled "Act Early, Live Life Shukhee" on 10 November 2026 at Telecom Bhaban.
Mohammad Solaimun Rasel, CTO and CBO of GHL, inaugurated the session. Md. Ashraful Hassan, Chairman, Grameen Group, attended as Chief Guest. He said, "Grameen's journey began with a belief in standing beside people. Today, that same belief is carrying us to the doorstep of healthcare. Through our eye hospitals, a person regains their sight; through safe sanitation, a family gets the foundation of a healthy life; and through digital initiatives like Shukhee, even people in remote villages receive quality medical care. We believe that only healthy people can build a prosperous society. Our commitment is to bring healthcare to every person through the power of social business." Dr. Ahmed Armaan Siddiqui, Chief Executive Officer of GHL/Shukhee, shared his vision of one ecosystem with a shared preventive health mission, from screening to measurable health outcomes. Mohammad Moinul Hakim, CEO of Experto ReWell, presented EverGreen Health™, LinX CGM and Whole-Body Digital Twin technology, showing how screening can lead to precision prevention.
An expert session was conducted by Prof. Dr. Md. Robed Amin, Professor of Medicine, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Prof. Dr. Md. Feroz Amin, Director, BIRDEM, Dr. Hurjahan Banu (Urmi), Associate Professor of Endocrinology and Metabolism, Bangladesh Medical University. Also present were Brig Gen Dr. Md. Jalal Uddin (Retd), Advisor to the Chairman, Grameen Telecom Trust and other high officials.

JnU announces admission test schedule for 2026-27 academic year
item.description:
Jagannath University (JnU) has announced the admission test schedule for first-year undergraduate (honours) and BBA programmes for the 2026-27 academic year.
Applications will open on November 25, while admission tests for five units will be held from January 1 to January 23.
The information was announced in an admission circular signed by JnU Acting Registrar Prof Dr Sheikh Md Gias Uddin on Wednesday.
According to the circular, applicants can submit their applications online from 12pm on November 25 until 11:59pm on December 10 through the university's admission website: https://admission.jnu.ac.bd .
The application fee has been set at Tk1,200 for Units A, B, C and D, and Tk1,500 for Unit E.
The admission test schedule is as follows:
All admission tests will be held from 10am to 11am.
According to the circular, students who passed their SSC or equivalent examinations in 2023 or 2024 and their HSC or equivalent examinations in 2026 will be eligible to apply, subject to meeting the prescribed requirements.
