item.title: Mir Mugdho memorial defaced again in Brahmanbaria
item.description:
A memorial dedicated to July uprising martyr Mir Mugdho in Chinair of Brahmanbaria Sadar upazila has been defaced with black paint again, obscuring much of his portrait and name.
Local resident and Jubo Dal leader Md Uzzal Ahmed confirmed the incident. He said he noticed the defacement on Wednesday afternoon, adding that the memorial had been similarly defaced before.
Ripan Das, inspector (investigation) of Brahmanbaria Sadar Police Station, said police visited the site after receiving reports of the incident.
He said police were investigating how the memorial was defaced and who was responsible.
On November 25, 2025, the memorial in Chinair was similarly defaced with black paint. However, those responsible for that incident were never identified.

item.title: Aminul joins Lahore Qalandars as high-performance advisor
Sakhawat: Bangladesh targets universal health coverage by 2030
item.description:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain has reaffirmed Bangladesh’s commitment to achieving universal health coverage (UHC) by 2030, saying the government is working to ensure essential healthcare for everyone, regardless of location or social status.
He made the remarks at the first BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Conference in Colombo, Sri Lanka, attended by health ministers, policymakers and experts from member countries.
Sakhawat highlighted progress in reducing maternal and neonatal mortality, maintaining the country’s polio-free status and expanding immunisation programs.
He said HPV vaccination coverage had risen from 2% to more than 85% since the formation of the new government, with a target of reaching full coverage by the end of November.
The minister said the government, under Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s leadership, had doubled the health sector budget to 1.01% of GDP, with plans to gradually raise it to 5%.
He outlined plans to strengthen preventive and primary healthcare, including establishing primary healthcare centres in more than 4,600 unions and upgrading upazila health complexes from 50 to 151 beds.
Other initiatives include introducing solar power at major government health facilities, improving medical waste management at 15 major hospitals and adopting the One Health approach.
The government is also working to introduce an integrated electronic health record system and unique e-Health IDs to digitise healthcare services.
To strengthen regional health security, Sakhawat proposed setting up a BIMSTEC Regional Genetic Disease Observatory and Early Warning System.
He stressed the importance of regional cooperation in tackling non-communicable diseases, climate-related health risks, antimicrobial resistance and pandemics, saying Bangladesh was ready to work with other member states through joint initiatives and knowledge-sharing.

item.title: Police seal Sylhet resort where fugitive ex-MP Ranjit held meeting
item.description:
Police have sealed Sohel Square Eco Resort in Ratargul, Gowainghat, Sylhet, after fugitive former Sunamganj-1 MP Ranjit Sarkar held a meeting there, triggering widespread controversy.
According to Gowainghat police, the resort was sealed on Wednesday.
Repeated calls to Gowainghat police station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Omar Faruk went unanswered. However, duty officer Sub-Inspector Hasib said the Sohel Square Resort in Ratargul was shut down by police around 3am.
Four people, including two resort employees and two Awami League leaders and activists, have been detained in connection with the incident. Police said preparations for filing a case were underway.
According to police and other sources, a lawyer rented the resort on November 8, claiming he would organise an educational tour. More than 150 people arrived at the venue by bus around 3pm and took part in various activities.
Ranjit, joint secretary of Sylhet district Awami League, later appeared at the resort, put up a separate banner, delivered a brief speech and left shortly afterwards.
In a video circulated on social media, he was heard saying that he had held a rally with party leaders and activists after entering the country. He also vowed to continue the struggle until Sheikh Hasina returned to Bangladesh and urged activists to prepare for a final fight.
Ranjit had been in hiding since August 5, 2024, and was reportedly staying in the United Kingdom for a period.
He uploaded the meeting's video to his Facebook account at 4:49pm on Monday. Hours after the footage went viral, an agitated group set fire to his house in Gopaltilla, Sylhet city.
Sunamganj police later arrested Tahirpur upazila Awami League Organising Secretary Tara Mia after identifying him in the video. He was subsequently sent to jail on a court order.
Sources said the meeting was organised under the leadership of local Awami League and Jubo League leaders, including Farid Ahmed Shamim, Aminur Rahman Chowdhury and Masuk Ahmed.
Meanwhile, Ranjit's whereabouts remain unknown. In a WhatsApp conversation with a news outlet, he claimed the meeting was held inside Bangladesh, in his electoral constituency, with only local residents attending.
Acknowledging that the Awami League was banned, he said party leaders would hold programmes wherever they found an opportunity.

item.title: Hasnat questions fertilizer dealership appointments over alleged nepotism
item.description:
Questions over alleged favoritism in the distribution of fertilizer dealerships have emerged after claims that relatives of sitting lawmakers were among those awarded dealerships under a nationwide appointment process.
Hasnat Abdullah, member of parliament for Comilla-4, alleged that the beneficiaries included the wives, sons, nieces and other relatives of sitting MPs, raising concerns over transparency in the selection process.
He said the appointment process was marked by unprecedented corruption and asked the agriculture minister whether it would be reconsidered.
The opposition MP raised the allegations in a supplementary question to the minister during Wednesday afternoon's parliamentary session, presided over by Deputy Speaker Barrister Kaiser Kamal.
Citing several newspaper headlines, Hasnat told the House: “An MP's son, brother-in-law and nephew's wife have become fertilizer dealers. In Thakurgaon, 28 of the 31 dealers are affiliated with the BNP, and 10 of them are wives, children and nieces of party leaders.”
He also noted that a Chhatra Dal leader had been fatally attacked in Natore and that a child of an MP was also alleged to have received a dealership.
Hasnat described the appointments as a “grand festival” of favoritism.
Addressing the minister, he asked whether the irregularities were premeditated, whether the appointments would be reviewed, and when MPs would cease to exploit their positions for the commercial benefit of themselves and their families.
Agriculture Minister Mohammad Amin Ur Rashid responded that 2 committees had been constituted to oversee the appointments: one at the upazila level, chaired by the Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO), and another at the district level, chaired by the Deputy Commissioner (DC).
He said applications had been invited under specified rules and conditions, and that the ministry had instructed both committees to adhere strictly to those rules.
According to the minister, applications were first forwarded to the upazila level, where the UNO-led committee, together with the upazila agriculture officer, the relevant local agriculture officer and local dignitaries, conducted the initial scrutiny.
The vetted proposals were then submitted to the DC's office, where the district committee reviewed them and sent a ranked list of 3 candidates to the ministry.
The ministry declared the first-ranked candidate the dealer.
The minister added that the district committee comprised the district agriculture officer, the DC and other relevant officials. All proposals reached the ministry bearing the signatures of every committee member rather than that of any single individual.

item.title: Tarique Rahman joins COP31 summit in Türkiye
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman joined the COP31 climate summit at the Antalya Exhibition Centre in Türkiye at 10:10am local time on Wednesday.
The prime minister’s Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu confirmed his participation, saying leaders and representatives from various countries were attending the summit.
Tarique is scheduled to attend the World Leaders Summit, followed by a Zero Waste Roundtable meeting. The summit is being chaired by Turkish Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change Minister Murat Kurum.
On the sidelines, the prime minister is scheduled to hold separate meetings with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Chinese Vice-President Han Zheng, Shiplu said.
In the evening, Tarique will attend a dinner hosted by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in honour of world leaders.
The prime minister arrived in Antalya from Dhaka on Tuesday to attend the summit. He is leading a high-level Bangladesh delegation and is accompanied by his wife, Zubaida Rahman.

item.title: Turkiye keen to send women’s health experts after Zubaida-Emine meeting
item.description:
Turkiye has expressed interest in strengthening cooperation with Bangladesh in several areas, including tackling the impacts of climate change, protecting the health of women and children, renewable energy and the production of eco-friendly products.
Turkiye’s First Lady Emine Erdogan has particularly expressed willingness to send a team of experts to Bangladesh to share experience and cooperate in addressing the health problems faced by women in the country’s coastal and marginalised areas due to climate change.
The matters were discussed at a meeting between Dr Zubaida Rahman, spouse of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, and Emine Erdogan, spouse of Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and also chairperson of the Zero Waste Foundation.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam disclosed this at a press conference held on Tuesday at the Conference Room of the Papillon Ziugma Relaxury Hotel in Antalya.
She said the highly fruitful meeting between Dr Zubaida Rahman and the Turkish First Lady took place on the first day of the Bangladesh delegation’s participation in the COP31 climate summit.
The two sides discussed in detail potential bilateral cooperation to tackle the impacts of climate change and its adverse effects on women and children.
Shama Obaed said Emine Erdogan praised the capacity and resilience of the people of Bangladesh in facing the adversities of climate change.
She also expressed interest in cooperating with Bangladesh on waste-to-energy production, solar power and other eco-friendly initiatives.
The meeting also discussed expanding the market for Bangladeshi jute products, especially eco-friendly and biodegradable ones, as an alternative to plastic, in Turkiye and other international markets. The Turkish First Lady showed particular interest in this area.
The state minister said Dr Zubaida Rahman highlighted women’s empowerment, the protection of women’s health, and the health and social problems being faced by women and children due to climate change in Bangladesh.
She also briefed the Turkish First Lady about various programmes undertaken by the government under the leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to build an eco-friendly Bangladesh, particularly tree plantation and the “Amar Khal Khanon” (digging my canal) programme.
Praising the initiatives, Emine Erdogan said there were wide scopes for cooperation between Bangladesh and Turkiye in energy production, use and export of jute products, women’s empowerment and tackling climate change.
Noting that the Rohingya crisis was also discussed at the meeting, Shama Obaed said Emine Erdogan had visited Bangladesh and the Rohingya camps in Cox’s Bazar in 2017, when the Rohingyas took shelter in Bangladesh.
The state minister said the Turkish government has been providing humanitarian assistance to the Rohingyas for a long time, adding that the only sustainable solution to the crisis is their safe, voluntary and dignified repatriation.
However, the meeting also stressed ensuring healthcare, education and other basic rights for the Rohingyas until they are repatriated. The Turkish First Lady assured that Turkiye would work with Bangladesh and continue providing necessary support in this regard.
Speaking about the impact of climate change on women and children, the state minister said women in Bangladesh’s coastal regions face constant challenges in adapting to hostile environmental conditions.
She said issues of internal displacement and health risks for women caused by climate change were also raised at the meeting.
According to her, Emine Erdogan expressed interest in sharing Turkiye’s experience in addressing these problems with Bangladesh. To this end, she wants to send a team of experts to Bangladesh, who will work with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
The two countries will exchange experience, particularly on addressing the health problems of marginalised women due to climate change and on improving maternal health.
Shama Obaed further said Dr Zubaida Rahman invited the Turkish First Lady to visit Bangladesh. Recalling her 2017 visit, Emine Erdogan also expressed her interest in visiting Bangladesh again and voiced hope of making the trip soon at a convenient time.

item.title: 33 BGB platoons deployed in Dhaka, Gazipur, Narayanganj
item.description:
A total of 33 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) have been deployed in industrial zones and key strategic points across Dhaka, Gazipur and Narayanganj to maintain law and order and prevent any untoward incidents.
The information was disclosed in a BGB press release issued on Wednesday.
According to the release, in Dhaka, one platoon has been deployed in Mirpur, two in Savar and Hemayetpur, two in Jirani, nine in Ashulia and two in Jamgara.
In Gazipur, one platoon has been deployed in Chandra, two in Palli Bidyut, one in Mouchak, one in Ambag-Kata, one in Kashimpur, one in Naojor, one in Bhogra Bypass, one in Gacha and one in Salna.
In Narayanganj, two platoons have been deployed at Shibu Market and Katherpul, two in Jalkuri, one at the BSCIC Industrial Estate, one at Chashara intersection and one in the Kanchpur Bridge and Shimrail areas.
Meanwhile, a monitoring cell at BGB headquarters is maintaining round-the-clock surveillance using live footage from drones, body-worn cameras and other specialised equipment.
The release added that field operations are being closely monitored and coordination among the relevant units is ongoing.

item.title: Police: Outsiders tried to stir unrest at Hemayetpur factories
item.description:
Police have dispersed outsiders who allegedly attempted to create unrest at several garment factories in Hemayetpur, Savar, with the situation now calm, a senior police official said on Wednesday.
Dhaka Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime, Operations and Traffic-North) Md Jahangir Alam made the remarks while briefing reporters on the workers’ protests in the area.
He said the situation had been peaceful since morning, but outsiders later tried to cause trouble at a few factories. Police dispersed them, although it was not clear whether they were garment workers.
Jahangir said the ongoing wage dispute had centred on the formation of a minimum wage board, which has already been established. Discussions have been held, and a decision is expected soon. He alleged that a third party was trying to exploit the situation for its own interests.
More than 100 police personnel from different units, including Industrial Police, APBn, Dhaka District Police, Detective Branch and Border Guard Bangladesh, have been deployed in the area, he said.
Refuting social media claims that police had opened fire and people had been killed, Jahangir said he was unaware of any use of lethal weapons by police since August 5. He said officers had instructions not to use such weapons and were applying only the minimum force necessary to maintain order.
He added that police intelligence units were monitoring possible attempts to destabilise the area, while the cyber security team was working to identify those spreading rumours to incite workers. Legal action would be taken against those found responsible, he said.

item.title: 44 more Bangladeshis deported from Europe
item.description:
Another 44 Bangladeshis who travelled to Europe through irregular channels or without proper documentation have been sent back home. Of them, 40 returned from Greece and four from Cyprus.
According to immigration police and airport sources, the returnees arrived at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at 9:15am on Wednesday on a special chartered flight (N05542).
At the airport, Brac's Migration Program, with support from Civil Aviation Security and the Probashi Kallyan Desk (Expatriates' Welfare Desk), provided the returnees with emergency assistance, counselling and financial support to help them reach their respective homes.
Representatives from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Probashi Kallyan Desk were also present.
Shariful Hasan, associate director of Brac's Migration Program and Youth Platform, confirmed that 44 Bangladeshis returned from Europe on Wednesday morning.
He said they received food and financial assistance at the airport under the Protyasha-2 project, jointly funded by the European Union (EU) and Brac. They will also receive further counselling, training and financial support.
Shariful Hasan said Bangladeshis had long topped the list of people entering Italy from Libya by crossing the Mediterranean Sea. According to this year's data, Bangladeshis also rank first among those entering Greece from Libya through the Mediterranean.
He warned that such dangerous sea journeys frequently result in loss of life, while European countries are tightening restrictions on irregular migration.
Under new migration policies, people entering Europe through irregular channels are being sent back promptly, with their asylum applications rejected, he said.
"Even after spending Tk30-40 lakh, the outcome is effectively zero. Yet many people believe that simply reaching Europe by any means necessary will solve all their problems. This misconception must be dispelled," he added.
Shariful Hasan also said one of the returnees had previously used TikTok to encourage others to travel from Bangladesh to Europe through irregular channels.
He urged prospective migrants to exercise caution, avoid dangerous sea routes and acquire the necessary skills to migrate through legal channels.
Earlier, on October 23, Brac reported that another 35 Bangladeshis had been sent back from Italy and Greece on a special flight.
In 2017, the Bangladesh government signed a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) agreement with several European countries concerning the return of undocumented and irregular Bangladeshi migrants.
Under the framework, around 5,000 Bangladeshis have returned home so far, many of them from Cyprus, Italy, Romania, France, Greece and Malta.
Shariful Hasan said the largest groups of Bangladeshis returning from Europe in recent years came from Italy, Greece and Germany.
Upon arrival, returnees receive emergency assistance and counselling at the airport, followed by economic support to help them rebuild their lives, he said.
He added that awareness campaigns were being conducted across the country to discourage risky migration, while European countries had also begun efforts to recruit Bangladeshi workers through legal and formal channels.

item.title: Grameen Bank office set on fire in Pabna
item.description:
Miscreants set fire to a Grameen Bank branch office at Dogachi Bazar in Pabna early Wednesday, damaging its signboard and front section.
According to locals, a group of youths chanting “Joy Bangla” slogans poured petrol on the office and set it ablaze around 12:30am.
Witnesses said the attackers first set fire to the bank's signboard, smashed the office's glass panels and then poured petrol on the front section before fleeing.
Night guard Abdul Wahab, who was inside the office, raised the alarm after seeing the flames. The property owner, bank employees and locals rushed to the scene and brought the fire under control, preventing major damage.
The assistant general manager of Grameen Bank's Pabna zonal office, Asaduzzaman, confirmed the incident, saying no important bank documents were damaged. The bank was preparing to file a complaint with police.
Pabna Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Tarikul Islam said a police patrol team visited the scene after receiving information about the incident. Police returned in the morning to collect evidence, and legal action was underway.

item.title: President urges global action for safe Rohingya repatriation, protection
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Wednesday called on the international community to take more effective measures for the safe repatriation of forcibly displaced Rohingyas sheltered in Bangladesh and for protecting vulnerable women and children.
The president made the call when Duchess of Edinburgh Sophie Helen Rhys-Jones paid a courtesy call on him at Bangabhaban.
During the meeting, the President said the Duchess’s visit carried a message of hope for the Rohingya people of Myanmar, particularly women and children, who are facing an uncertain future.
He said her visit to the Rohingya camps would play an important role in drawing greater international attention to the humanitarian crisis.
The president said the protracted Rohingya crisis was putting immense socioeconomic and environmental pressure on densely populated Bangladesh while also raising concerns over regional security.
President Fakhrul welcomed the Duchess to Bangladesh and praised her longstanding contributions to women’s dignity and empowerment, eye health and the development of young people.
Referring to Bangladesh’s longstanding friendly relations with the UK, he said Bangladesh remained committed to further advancing bilateral ties based on mutual respect and shared interests.
During the meeting, they also discussed increasing British investment in Bangladesh, improving the education system and expanding women’s participation in sports, among other issues.
The Duchess shared her experiences during her three-day visit to Bangladesh, including visits to the Rohingya camps in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh Krira Shikkha Protisthan (BKSP) and the Bangladesh Institute of Peace Support Operation Training (BIPSOT).
She praised Bangladesh’s progress in advancing and empowering women and their contribution to the country’s economic development.
The president expressed hope that the Duchess’s visit would further strengthen the existing friendly relations and cooperation between Bangladesh and the UK.
Senior officials from the President’s Office and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the British High Commissioner and members of the Duchess’s delegation were present during the meeting.

item.title: Cargo lorry set on fire in Narayanganj
item.description:
Miscreants set fire to the wheels of a parked cargo lorry in the Jalkuri area of Narayanganj on Tuesday night.
No casualties were reported.
The incident occurred around midnight in the Koraitola area of Jalkuri along the Dhaka-Narayanganj Link Road.
According to local sources, miscreants poured petrol on the lorry's wheels and set them on fire before fleeing the scene.
The driver and his helper managed to extinguish the flames using a fire extinguisher kept in the vehicle. However, part of the lorry's tyres was damaged in the incident.
Additional Superintendent of Police in Narayanganj, Tarek Al Mehedi, confirmed the incident, saying miscreants were responsible.
He added that police would examine footage from nearby CCTV cameras to identify those involved and bring them to justice.

item.title: Worker-police clashes keep Savar, Ashulia industrial belt tense; several factories shut
item.description:
Garment workers at several factories in Dhaka's Savar and Ashulia industrial belts continued protesting on Wednesday, demanding a higher minimum wage after several days of unrest.
At one point, some protesters took to the streets and attempted to block roads, triggering clashes and chases between workers and police. Tensions spread across several parts of the industrial belt.
Workers entered factories and joined their shifts as usual in the morning in Hemayetpur, Savar, and Jamgora, Ashulia. However, workers at several factories in the two areas later staged work stoppages to press for their demands.
Around 9:30am, authorities at several factories in Jamgora announced holidays following the workers' work stoppages. As workers left the factories and attempted to block roads, police fired tear gas and sound grenades to disperse them.
Several rounds of clashes and chases between police and workers followed.
A similar situation unfolded in Hemayetpur, Savar, shortly after 10am. Workers from several factories came out and gathered on the streets, attempting to block roads. Police fired tear gas to disperse them.
No casualties had been reported in the incidents as of the time of filing this report.
However, an Industrial Police source said that despite the unrest at several factories, production remained normal at most garment factories across the industrial belt.
Attempts to contact Industrial Police-1 Superintendent of Police Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan several times for details on the overall situation and the exact number of factories that had declared holidays were unsuccessful.

item.title: Two women killed as bus runs them over in Gabtoli
item.description:
Two women were killed and another person was injured after being hit by a bus in the Gabtoli area under Darus Salam police station in the capital on Wednesday.
The identities of the victims have not yet been established.
The accident occurred around 10:30am near Gabtoli Bus Terminal.
Darus Salam Police Station Sub-Inspector Diraj Nandi said the women were crossing the road near the terminal when a Chandni Paribahan bus travelling from Bogra to Dhaka ran them over.
Two women died on the spot, while another person was injured.
He said the bodies of the deceased and the injured person were taken to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital.
The bus was seized and its driver detained in connection with the incident, the police official added.

item.title: Titas Commuter train bogie set on fire at Akhaura station, 2 detained
item.description:
A bogie of the Titas Commuter train was set on fire while parked for shunting at Akhaura Railway Station in Brahmanbaria early Wednesday, damaging 11 seats.
Flammable substances, suspected to be petrol or diesel, were also found on seats in an adjacent bogie.
Two people have been detained by the Railway Nirapotta Bahini (RNB) for questioning in connection with the incident.
The fire broke out around 3:40am on Wednesday on a shunting line beside the Railway Government High School, on the northern side of the station.
According to railway sources, the Dhaka-bound Titas Commuter train had been placed on the shunting line after completing its washing operations when unidentified individuals set fire to the carriage marked ‘Ta’.
On receiving the information, station officials, RNB members, Ansar personnel and Fire Service members rushed to the scene and brought the fire under control.
The fire damaged seven two-seater and four four-seater seats in the carriage. Meanwhile, a substance suspected to be petrol or diesel was found splashed on seats in the adjacent carriage marked ‘Ja’.
Officials said a major loss was averted as the fire was brought under control quickly.
Following the incident, RNB members conducted a raid in the washing facility area and detained two suspects, identified as Runi, 26, and Morshalin, 18. Both are from Cumilla. They were later handed over to Akhaura Railway Police Station.
The incident delayed the Titas Commuter train's departure for Dhaka by around one and a half hours.
Akhaura Railway Police Station Officer-in-Charge Abdul Quddus said efforts were underway to identify and detain those involved in the incident. Legal action was also being taken in connection with the case.

item.title: Bus set on fire in front of Mirpur zoo
item.description:
Miscreants set fire to a Chiriyakhana City Paribahan bus parked in front of the National Zoo in the capital’s Mirpur area early Wednesday.
Sub-Inspector Md Ripon, duty officer at Shah Ali Police Station, confirmed the incident at 2:20am on Wednesday.
He said miscreants set fire to the bus parked beside the zoo at around 1am.
“Several teams of police are at the scene,” he added.
Rashed Bin Khaled of the Fire Service and Civil Defence control room said a fire service team reached the spot at around 1:19am after receiving information about the incident. However, the fire had already been extinguished by locals before the team arrived.
Video footage shows several Chiriyakhana City Paribahan buses parked at the location, with one of them engulfed in flames. Several buses parked beside the burning vehicle were quickly moved away.

item.title: Winter’s early signs emerge in northern districts as cold-related illnesses rise
item.description:
A blanket of fog has begun covering parts of northern Bangladesh in the early morning, while a slight chill in the air signals the gradual transition towards winter.
Over the past week, residents of Rangpur, Lalmonirhat, Kurigram, Nilphamari and Gaibandha have noticed foggy mornings, although temperatures remain relatively mild and sunshine still brings some warmth during the day.
But the changing weather is already taking a toll on public health, with hospitals in the region reporting a growing number of patients suffering from cold-related illnesses, including fever, coughs and respiratory infections.
At Rangpur Medical College Hospital, 382 patients were admitted with cold-related illnesses over the past week, said its Director, Brigadier Ashikur Rahman.
At Rangpur Railway Station, where some people take shelter, Moksed Ali says the cold is still manageable, but the mornings are becoming increasingly uncomfortable.
“It is not very cold yet, but there is a slight chill in the morning. Fog covers the surroundings, and the cold seems to be gradually setting in,” he said.
Another person taking shelter at the station, Asia Khatun, said even a little cold wind makes life difficult for people without adequate winter clothing.
“When the wind blows, we feel cold and suffer a lot. There is some fog in the early morning, but the sun usually appears after 7am, bringing some relief. As the days pass, we are becoming increasingly worried about the coming winter. We do not even have warm clothes,” she said.
The changing weather is also affecting people who have to remain outdoors for work.
Rafiqul Islam, a truck driver from Kaliganj in Lalmonirhat, said dense fog often blankets the roads from early morning until around 6:30am, forcing drivers to use headlights and exercise extra caution.
He said visibility becomes poor during these hours, although the weather remains relatively comfortable once the sun comes out.
The seasonal transition is also drawing the attention of farmers, whose livelihoods depend heavily on weather conditions.
Across the Rangpur region, farmers are preparing to harvest Aman paddy, while many are busy bringing the crop home and tending winter vegetables.
They are keeping a close watch on morning fog and fluctuations in temperature, concerned about their possible effects on crops.
Krishab Chandra Roy, a farmer from Kakina in Kaliganj, said dense fog over the past week had made him somewhat reluctant to head to the fields early in the morning.
“It is difficult to work in the fields when there is so much fog early in the morning. However, the sun usually comes out after 7am, and it does not feel very cold then,” he said.
He fears temperatures may drop further across the region in the coming days.
The approaching winter is also bringing business to seasonal clothing markets, although sales have yet to reach their peak.
Moslem Uddin, a winter clothing trader on Station Road in Rangpur, said shopkeepers had started stocking up on sweaters, shawls, blankets and other winter essentials.
“Traders like me have opened our shops with winter clothes, and sales have started. But business has not yet picked up fully,” he said.
While people are preparing for the seasonal change, health concerns are becoming increasingly evident, particularly among children and older people.
Doctors say sudden fluctuations in temperature can increase the risk of respiratory illnesses, urging families to take extra care of vulnerable members.
Dr Tanvir Ahmed, a paediatrician at Rangpur Medical College Hospital, said the number of children seeking treatment had been increasing every day amid the changing weather.
Many children are suffering from fever and pneumonia, he said, advising parents to ensure proper care and take necessary precautions to protect them from the cold.
Weather officials say the gradual fall in morning temperatures and changing atmospheric conditions are contributing to the formation of fog across the region.
Mostafizar Rahman, an assistant meteorologist at the Rangpur Meteorological Office, said differences between day and night temperatures, along with fluctuations in weather conditions, were creating favourable conditions for fog formation.
He said fog was developing in the early morning after prolonged cloudy conditions, particularly when clouds cleared and the sky became relatively open.
The changing activity of the seasonal monsoon is also influencing the weather pattern, he added.
Some parts of the Rangpur region may experience a slight chill within the next 15 days, with a possibility of a mild cold wave, he said.
Rangpur Divisional Commissioner Jahangir Alam said adequate winter clothing had been kept ready in every upazila of the division for distribution among poor, homeless and vulnerable people as temperatures begin to fall.

Motorcyclist killed in collision with oil tanker in Dhaka
item.description:
A 28-year-old motorcyclist was killed after an oil tanker belonging to Asia Pump hit his motorcycle in the capital’s Khilkhet area on Wednesday morning.
The accident occurred around 10am near the Khilkhet police box, said Habibur Rahman, an inspector at the Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) police outpost.
Selim, who was riding the motorcycle with the victim, Tausif, said the tanker struck them from behind, leaving Tausif critically injured.

item.title: Commerce minister: Govt to support reopening of closed Savar tanneries
item.description:
The government will provide necessary technical and financial assistance to tanneries at Savar that have yet to begin production after relocation from Hazaribagh, Commerce Minister Khandaker Abdul Muktadir said on Wednesday.
He also said the government has prioritised environmental compliance, modern waste management and international certification to enhance the global competitiveness of Bangladesh's leather industry.
The minister made the remarks while speaking at the inauguration of the Bangladesh-Netherlands Sustainable Trade Forum 2026 and the CBI Home Textiles and Leather Programme at a hotel in the capital, said a PID handout.
The event was jointly organised by the Netherlands' Centre for the Promotion of Imports from Developing Countries (CBI) and LightCastle Partners.
The minister also warned that no tannery failing to meet environmental regulations will be allowed to operate.
Muktadir said Bangladesh has significant potential in exporting leather and leather goods, noting that the country exported products worth around $1.78 billion in leather and non-leather categories last year.
He identified the European Union as an important and promising market for Bangladesh, while neighbouring India has also emerged as a major buyer of Bangladeshi leather products.
He stressed the need to ensure product quality, environmental compliance and production systems that meet international market requirements.
Referring to the prolonged relocation of tanneries from Hazaribagh to Hemayetpur in Savar, the minister said the delay had hindered the development of the leather sector.
The government is now taking effective initiatives to address the sector's existing problems.
He said every factory with an area of 50,000 square feet or more would be required to install its own effluent treatment plant (ETP).
The minister said initiatives were also being taken to enhance the capacity of the Central Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP) at the Savar Tannery Industrial Estate and install an improved chromium recovery unit to make waste management more effective.
Once implemented, these measures would help Bangladesh's leather industry strengthen its position in international markets, he added.
Highlighting the importance of the cottage, micro, small and medium enterprises (CMSMEs) sector, Muktadir said its development was essential for inclusive economic growth, employment generation and reducing income inequality.
The sector currently contributes less than one-fourth of the country's gross domestic product (GDP), he said, stressing the need to raise its contribution to at least 60 percent to reduce economic disparities.
Emphasising the need to remove financing barriers for small entrepreneurs, the minister said many promising entrepreneurs were being deprived of necessary funds due to complicated documentation and procedural hurdles in obtaining bank loans.
On Bangladesh-Netherlands trade relations, the minister said cooperation between the two countries could create new opportunities in sustainable industrialisation, technology transfer, skills development and expanded access to international markets.
He said the Netherlands' technological and institutional expertise could play an important role in making Bangladesh's export-oriented sectors, particularly home textiles and leather, more competitive.
He also appreciated the support extended by the Dutch government, CBI and development partners for the development of Bangladesh's SME and leather sectors.
The CBI Home Textiles and Leather Programme was also inaugurated at the event, focusing on capacity development, compliance with international standards and expanding export opportunities.
Dutch Ambassador to Bangladesh Joris van Bommel and CBI Managing Director Judith Arends also spoke at the event.
Representatives from the public and private sectors, development partners, entrepreneurs and other stakeholders attended the programme.

When lies go viral
item.description:
Today, people can hardly avoid social networking sites, smartphones, and the wider online environment. This growing vulnerability can distort public debate and weaken social trust. Human perception is psychological and develops through daily reactions to events, statements, and rumours. It is now shaped not just by oratory, print media, and television, but by a faster, more affective information landscape.
Often, fraudulent claims are presented as credible as Facebook posts, YouTube videos, TikTok snippets, fabricated news cards, and AI- generated material compete for attention. In Bangladesh, this risk has become clearer during political transition, election-related mobilization, student politics and debates over national sovereignty.
Information warfare and the cognitive battlefield
NATO's scientific advisory body describes cognitive warfare as manipulating an opponent's cognition to weaken the will and ability to make decisions. There are no boundaries in the conflict of information warfare. It entails manipulating, warping, magnifying, or suppressing information to affect public opinion. The parts of the human mind -- emotion, memory, fear, values and judgement -- are the primary targets.
The human mind therefore becomes the battlefield. The objective is not always to persuade individuals to believe a particular lie. A more effective objective may be to induce confusion. This undermines reasoned discussion and makes emotionally fulfilling narratives more appealing than substantiated facts.
In Bangladesh, information warfare typically operates in tandem, using multiple linked approaches:
Is Bangladesh at risk?
There is a large and active online population in Bangladesh, which is especially vulnerable to the issues of political polarization, social and religious sensitivities, and media literacy gap.
Information can be false and proliferate from platform to platform before being verified by authorities. Stories of religion, nationalism, violence, and social grievance can easily foster fear and anger, division and distrust.
Social media has great advantages to it. It provides rapid information, gives a voice to the voiceless, and uncovers the truth, where traditional media may fail. However, Facebook is also a hub for misinformation in Bangladesh due to this openness.
Rumour Scanner reported 4,195 instances of misinformation in 2025, which was approximately 30% percent higher than in 2024, out of which 3,806 were found on Facebook. It also recorded a highest monthly total of 521 cases in December 2025, 86% of which were political cases.
A malicious rumour can easily and rapidly break out from the screen and become a real threat. Accusations and reactions can be triggered well before the truth is known, by false allegations of religious insult, communities, child abductions, or even political conspiracies that can provoke crowds.
That is why it is not just what people believe which is dangerous, but what their beliefs can trigger.
It can be a community reaction -- fear of a neighbourhood, hostility between communities, pressure on public institutions, or lack of trust in public institutions.
The psychological damage may have occurred by the time that a rectification is supplied.
The layers of AI
Artificial intelligence has blurred the line between real and fabricated content online. AI-generated videos, manipulated images, and convincing fake messages can appear authentic, prompting people to believe and share them before checking the facts.
Before the February 2026 election, researchers found many AI-manipulated posts intended to mislead voters. Some invented events that never occurred; others used fake images or news cards designed to resemble genuine journalism.
Deepfake videos also showed political leaders making statements they had never made. Female candidates were targeted with sexually explicit fake images, while other AI content attempted to create fear between religious communities.
The real peril of AI is not that every machine-generated image will fool everyone, but that it has dramatically lowered the cost of producing convincing deception.
Once, creating a realistic fake video required specialized equipment, technical expertise, and substantial effort. Nowadays, there are tools that can create a fake voice, image or short video within minutes.
For ordinary users, and even for professional fact-checkers, the amount of suspicious content can be very difficult to identify. It also helps a malicious actor to dismiss true evidence as a deepfake, as the researchers call it, and therefore to benefit from a more general “liar's dividend.”
Cross-border relations exist as a challenge to it. In 2025, Rumour Scanner reported 155 cases of disinformation regarding Bangladesh that was spread by external media and social media accounts. The information battle is not restricted within the country’s boundaries, but the narratives from external sources affect the minds and psychology of Bangladeshis.
Misinformation, disinformation and malinformation
The terms are interchangeable, but the difference is important. Misinformation is inaccurate information or information that is false, but not necessarily done with purposeful intent. A person who sends a re-posted old flood video that purports to be from the current disaster, could be spreading misinformation.
Disinformation is information that is knowingly and intentionally false for the purpose of deceiving, influencing or harming someone. An example is a fabricated quote by a political leader.
Malinformation is factual information that has been taken out of its context to mislead, harm or sway, which includes revealing private information to intimidate.
A coordinated entity may create deception, and the general citizen may then disseminate misinformation, believing it to be truthful. An original picture can have a deceptive caption, turning a reality into a tool for deceit.
Recognizing these variations will enable the community to react intelligently. Not all incorrect information is from an enemy, it can be every unverified share that can reinforce a harmful campaign.
A theory of the origins of false beliefs
As psychology demonstrates, people tend to see, validate, and share what confirms their political, religious, or social opinions. They may not accept corrective information, as it threatens them with an attack on their identity or community.
Emotion intensifies the issue. Fear, indignation, and outrage reduces fact-checking. Therefore, rumours generally incite violence, religious feuds, threats to women, and children, or national sovereignty.
These are statements that are meant to develop feelings, not thinking. The message “share before it is deleted” or “the media will not show you this” creates an urgency and does not give time to think.
Repeatedly seeing a claim on Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, and message groups may lead to a false impression of truth. People are seeing what they already believe in, as like-minded pages and online groups form echo chambers. Fake news has a reach that is greater than fact-checks.
Lessons from the Bangladesh Army
Bangladesh Army regularly observes October of each year as Cyber Security Awareness Month. Various awareness programs, seminars, workshops, and training take place during this month, more than in any other month.
All offices and installations use the slogan on cyber protection on top of the letters issued or circulated. Instructions on security breaches through social media, awareness against misinformation, disinformation, and malinformation are circulated and communicated to everybody regularly in each darbar, central motivational parade, and so on.
Thus, individuals are now more aware, and they are encouraged to report a security breach whenever it has been noticed.
The shared responsibility and the way forward
Independent fact-checking organizations like Rumor Scanner and FactWatch provide a valuable public record of false claims. Before a correction is issued, a deepfake video may reach a very large audience.
Thus, an effective response is necessary, and it must be timely and transparent. The news outlets should have verification desks and make clear corrections to readers and indicate how they were reached. We also need technology platforms to make synthetic content transparent and take effective action against concerted efforts of manipulation.
However, citizens too have a critical role to play in controlling misinformation. There must be questions asked before sharing a sensational post like: Who published it first? Do credible sources support the claim? Is the post evidence or an incitement to anger and urgency? A reverse image search, a fact check of the original source, or a fact check on a trusted fact-checking website can often prevent false information from spreading. Cognitive warfare in Bangladesh will continue, but public resistance can render manipulation much less effective. AI could be utilized to identify suspicious content at the earliest. Platforms, journalists, fact-checkers, and authorities can take a coordinated approach to verify them based on common guidelines. Media literacy and responsible journalism are also essential to public trust and these are tools that can help to enhance the response.
Colonel ASM Nazmul Haque, psc is in the Bangladesh Army.

item.title: Osmani Udyan reopens after 9yrs: Has Dhaka lost its green refuge?
item.description:
After remaining closed for nearly nine years, Osmani Udyan in the capital has reopened following a Tk147 crore renovation. The park now features new entrances, water bodies, walking paths, recreational facilities and a memorial to the July uprising.
However, the makeover has raised questions about whether Dhaka residents have regained their familiar green retreat or whether much of its natural character has been lost to concrete.
Owned by Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC), the 23-acre park is located between the Bangladesh secretariat and Nagar Bhaban. It has long served as a green refuge amid the traffic and crowds of Gulistan.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman inaugurated the renovated park and the July memorial on October 19. It opened to the public the following day.
The main entrance, opposite the Police Headquarters, has been rebuilt with two concrete gates shaped like the number 24 to commemorate the 2024 uprising. Inside, visitors will find fountains, water bodies, paved walkways, seating areas and elevated paths. The park has around 3.1km of walking routes.
However, the extensive use of concrete has drawn attention. Former dirt tracks have been replaced with paved paths, while concrete structures have been added around the water bodies.
Eden College student Nadia, who visited with a friend, welcomed the reopening but said the library, food court and health centre should open soon to make the park more lively.
Named after General MA G Osmani, commander-in-chief of the Liberation War, the park was once divided into 11 sections to commemorate the war's 11 sectors. It featured two small lakes, walking paths, sculptures and an auditorium.
Its historic Mughal-era cannon, Bibi Mariam, which had been a major attraction near the entrance, has been relocated beside the renovated Dhaka Gate.
The park earned the name “lungs of Dhaka” partly through a civic movement in the late 1990s, when environmentalists, teachers, writers and citizens protested a plan to build an international conference centre there. Their campaign sought to protect around 11,000 trees, and the plan was eventually scrapped.
Despite later plantation initiatives, many mature trees were felled during development work. Urban planners have also alleged that the renovation did not comply with building regulations, which allow structures to cover a maximum of 5% of a park's area.
The Tk108 crore main redevelopment project included boundary walls, a city museum, a library, 12 shops, a gymnasium, parking facilities, renovated lake banks and walkways. Five new water bodies, a children's play area, indoor games facilities, public toilets and a rainwater storage system were also included.
A 90-foot July memorial has been built over nearly one acre. The bronze structure carries the names of 834 people killed in the 2024 uprising, alongside 20 symbolic tombstones. Relief sculptures depict major events in the country's history, from the Language Movement to the July uprising.
However, the museum, library, gymnasium, parking area and food shops are not yet operational. DSCC says the remaining work may take another two months.
The park has various tree species, including mango, jackfruit, tamarind, banyan, neem and rain tree. But visitors say the loss of mature trees has reduced its greenery.
Old Dhaka businessman Osman Gani, who visited with a friend, said many large trees had been cut down.
“The greenery that once existed is no longer there. It used to feel cool when we came here, but now it feels hot,” he said, adding that newly planted trees would take years to mature.
Another concern is the introduction of a Tk10 entry fee. Abul Hasan, who visited with his wife and three children, questioned the charge, saying the park should remain free for ordinary people, including those who come for morning walks.
The park is open daily from 7am to 6pm.
The redevelopment project was taken up in late 2017, and work began in January 2018 with a 10-month completion target. The original contractor's agreement was cancelled in 2022 over alleged delays and contractual issues. PF Corporation was appointed in September 2023, but the project again missed its deadline.
The initial estimated cost of Tk54-58 crore eventually rose to Tk108 crore for the main project. Another Tk39 crore was spent on the memorial and entrance gates, taking the total to around Tk147 crore.
At the inauguration, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman stressed the need to minimise environmental damage in development projects.
Preserving the remaining trees, expanding greenery, completing unfinished facilities and ensuring public access remain key challenges for DSCC.

item.title: Two injured in Ashulia worker-police clash, 20 factories shut
item.description:
At least two garment workers were injured in a clash with police in Ashulia, Savar, on Tuesday morning as workers took to the streets demanding higher wages.
The clash broke out around 10:30am on the Baipail-Abdullahpur road in the Jamgora area, triggering chases and counter-chases between workers and police.
Police fired tear gas shells and sound grenades to bring the situation under control. Following the unrest, authorities declared holidays at 20 garment factories in the area.
According to police and local sources, most workers joined their respective factories at the scheduled time in the morning. However, workers at several factories stopped working and remained idle.
At one stage, workers blocked the road in Jamgora to press home their demand for higher wages. Tensions escalated when police tried to clear the blockade, leading to clashes and exchanges of brickbats between the two sides.
The injured workers were identified as Alamgir Hossain, 30, a finishing operator, and Razia Begum, 40, a sewing operator at Sterling Styles Limited.
Harun Or Rashid, operations manager of Ashulia Women and Children Hospital, said the two workers were taken to the hospital with injuries suspected to have been caused by rubber bullets.
"Razia Begum's injuries were serious, so she was referred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital. Alamgir received primary treatment and later left the hospital," he said.
However, police denied firing rubber bullets to disperse the protesters.
Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of police of Ashulia Industrial Police-1, said around noon that police had initially tried to persuade the workers to withdraw their blockade.
"When that failed, we used tear gas shells and sound grenades. No other weapons were used. If any workers were injured, they may have been hit by brickbats. No rubber bullets were fired," he said.
He added that authorities had declared holidays at around 20 factories in Ashulia amid the unrest.
Meanwhile, Khairul Mamun, legal affairs secretary of the Bangladesh Garments and Sweaters Workers Trade Union Centre, called for building trust among workers to resolve the ongoing dispute.
He said workers' concerns over wage increases could have been largely addressed if factory owners had promptly submitted their proposals to the wage board.
"Many factory owners are threatening to shut down their factories if workers refuse to work and warning them of possible job losses. The situation can be resolved by creating an atmosphere of trust among workers," he said.

item.title: Dr Khalilur outlines three key priorities for COP31
item.description:
UNGA President and Bangladesh foreign minister Dr Khalilur Rahman has outlined three key priorities for the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, calling for accelerated clean energy transition, predictable climate finance and stronger measures to protect vulnerable communities.
In a video message ahead of the global climate conference, Rahman stressed the need to translate longstanding international climate commitments into concrete action, particularly as climate-vulnerable countries continue to face increasingly severe consequences of global warming.
Highlighting his first priority, the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) President called for the effective implementation of commitments made under the Paris Agreement through faster deployment of clean energy, increased electrification and substantial reductions in greenhouse gas emissions.
He said that more than a decade after the adoption of the landmark climate accord, the international community must move beyond pledges and focus on delivering measurable results.
Identifying climate finance as his second priority, the Bangladesh diplomat emphasised the need to ensure predictable and accessible funding for climate adaptation, resilience-building and addressing loss and damage caused by climate-related disasters.
He underscored the importance of ensuring that financial resources reach countries and communities most vulnerable to climate change, enabling them to strengthen their capacity to withstand its growing impacts.
Rahman identified protecting human lives as his third priority, stressing the need for greater investment in early warning systems, disaster preparedness and community-level protection measures.
Such investments were essential to safeguarding vulnerable populations already experiencing the consequences of extreme weather events and other climate-related hazards, he added.
The UNGA president stressed that international climate action must prioritise practical measures that protect communities while accelerating the global transition towards a low-carbon and climate-resilient future.
The Paris Agreement, adopted in 2015, established a global framework for limiting temperature rise, strengthening climate resilience and mobilising financial support for developing countries.
However, implementation gaps, inadequate climate financing and the growing frequency of climate-related disasters continue to pose major challenges to achieving its objectives.

item.title: Law minister: 24,013 harassment cases withdrawn so far
item.description:
A total of 24,013 cases filed for political reasons and to harass individuals have been withdrawn so far, Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman has told parliament.
He disclosed the information during the question-and-answer session on the second day of the fourth session of the National Parliament, presided over by Speaker Major (retd) Hafiz Uddin Ahmed.
The minister was responding to a written question from Md Keramat Ali, MP for Chapainawabganj-1.
In his question, Keramat Ali said thousands of people were still facing harassment as various allegedly false and politically motivated cases filed during the previous regime remained unresolved. He sought an explanation for the delay in disposing of the cases and asked whether the government had a roadmap for resolving them.
In response, Asaduzzaman said the process of withdrawing politically motivated harassment cases began during the interim government. After taking office, the current government took initiatives to accelerate and streamline the process.
As part of the initiative, a four-member committee headed by the district magistrate was formed in each district on March 5, 2026.
The committees review applications for withdrawal, along with the First Information Report (FIR), charge sheet, where applicable, and the opinion of the public prosecutor.
They assess whether a case was filed to politically harass someone, whether its continuation serves the public interest and whether proceeding with it could compromise the state's interests before making recommendations for withdrawal.
The minister said a six-member central committee, with him as its convener, was formed on March 8 to coordinate the process and review recommendations from the district-level committees.
He added that the government would take necessary steps to withdraw a case once an application was received and the relevant district committee recommended its withdrawal on the grounds that it had been filed for harassment.

item.title: Murder accused escapes from Dhaka court after removing handcuffs
item.description:
An accused in the murder case of garment worker Alo Akter has escaped from a Dhaka court after removing his handcuffs.
The accused, Md Kawsar Mia, fled from the dock of the Dhaka First Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court, presided over by Acting Judge Mosaddeq Minhaj, on Tuesday.
Inspector Mohsin Hossain of the court's prosecution division confirmed the matter.
"Kawsar removed his handcuffs and fled from the dock around 12:40pm," he said.
Constable Arafat, who was responsible for escorting Kawsar to and from the court, said the accused was handcuffed while standing in the dock.
"The accused was handcuffed while standing in the dock. I went to the front of the courtroom to take custody of him, and he took advantage of my absence to remove his handcuffs and flee," he said.
The case is currently at the witness examination stage, with Tuesday scheduled for recording testimony. Kawsar, who had been in jail since his arrest, was brought to court for the hearing.
However, no witnesses appeared before the court. The next date for recording testimony has been set for January 28, court bench assistant Riaz Hossain said.
Alo was stabbed to death in a bathroom at her home in the Dakshin Para area of Dakshinkhan on July 20, 2020.
The following day, her father, Robiul Islam, filed a murder case with Dakshinkhan Police Station against unidentified suspects. Police arrested Kawsar from the Tongi area on the same day while investigating the case. The following day, he gave a confessional statement before a court, admitting to the murder.
In his statement, Kawsar said he had been in a romantic relationship with Alo for about a year. However, she had started avoiding him shortly before the incident. He later learned that she was involved with another man and had been refusing to speak to him.
According to his statement, Kawsar waited outside Alo's house on July 20, 2020. Around 9pm, he saw her to go the bathroom. When she came out and went to fetch a bucket from her room, he stopped her and tried to talk to her.
After Alo refused to speak to him, he stabbed her in the chest and back with a knife, according to his confessional statement.
Following the investigation, Sub-Inspector Sujan Chandra Karmakar of Dakshinkhan Police Station submitted a charge sheet against Kawsar on June 30, 2021.
The court framed charges against him on July 20, 2022, and subsequently began the trial.
So far, two witnesses, Alo's father, Robiul Islam, and her elder sister, Rabbina Akter, have testified in the case. Kawsar had been in custody since his arrest.

item.title: Holding the world accountable for the climate crisis
Iran says two oil tankers on fire in Hormuz
item.description:
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said Tuesday that two oil tankers were on fire in the Strait of Hormuz, where the country regularly targets ships that transit without its authorization.
Since the outbreak of the Middle East war in late February, Tehran has heavily restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use routes authorized by the Islamic Republic.
The United States has in response imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil.
“Two violating oil tankers, travelling along an unauthorized route in the Strait of Hormuz, have been brought to a halt following massive explosions and are left burning,” the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of Iran’s military, said in a statement.
The Guards did not specify the names or origins of the tankers.
Tehran has made multiple announcements in recent weeks saying ships had caught fire in the strait.
It has said some vessels struck mines, but the US military recently claimed all mines had been cleared from the waterway.
US Central Command, which oversees American military operations in the region, also said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.
On Tuesday, the Guards said “one of the vessels -- a super tanker -- struck a naval mine, resulting in an explosion.”
“The second tanker, which was under the escort of the aggressor American military and attempting a covert passage via an illegal route, also had an incident,” they added.

item.title: Explosions heard in Saudi capital Riyadh
item.description:
Multiple explosions were heard in the Saudi capital on Tuesday, as the military coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis said it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched by the Iran-backed group towards Riyadh.
AFP journalists heard the blasts and residents received an alert on their mobile phones instructing them to take shelter due to an “aerial threat.”
“Air defenses intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh,” the Saudi-led coalition posted on X.
A subsequent message from the country’s civil defense agency said the danger had passed.
The coalition had earlier said air defenses also destroyed a ballistic missile headed towards the southern region overnight.
Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest oil exporter, has faced near-daily strikes from the Houthis for weeks, after a truce in their long-running conflict unraveled in July.
On Sunday, the Houthis claimed attacks on Riyadh’s business district, where witnesses said the Aramco Tower was damaged.
Saudi authorities said the building suffered minor damage from falling shrapnel after an “attempted attack.”
Images released by Saudi Arabia’s press agency on Tuesday showed the Riyadh region’s deputy governor and other officials inspecting the building, with visible damage to some of its floors.
The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Aramco tankers, refineries, storage areas and the company’s headquarters.
The coalition has in response been launching airstrikes against Houthi positions inside Yemen.
According to Houthi news agency Saba, Saudi warplanes on Tuesday carried out a series of strikes on the capital Sanaa and its outskirts, targeting a gas facility and a building belonging to the Yemeni state oil company.
The coalition initially began fighting the Houthis in March 2015, months after the group seized Sanaa and forced out Yemen’s internationally recognized government.

item.title: US calls for ‘new’ Europe security framework as Russia-Ukraine talks open
item.description:
US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine on ending more than four years of war opened in Abu Dhabi Tuesday, with Washington calling for a “new” security framework, as Europe fears US President Donald Trump plans a deal with Moscow on the continent’s future.
Russian and Ukrainian negotiators sat facing each other, with Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner and business partner Steve Witkoff at the head of the table.
Kyiv’s delegation -- headed by intelligence chief Rustem Umerov -- met the US envoys as well as European and Nato officials ahead of negotiations.
Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine has killed hundreds of thousands. As another winter of war approaches, Ukraine and its European allies fear Washington will force Kyiv to accept a de facto defeat.
Trump has also floated a deal with Russia on rewriting Europe’s post-war security.
As the talks opened, Kushner said the US hoped to “create the right security relationships between Ukraine and Russia and Europe so that not only we end this war, we create a new framework and a new understanding” that will secure “decades, if not centuries, of peace.”
He conceded there was a “lot of intense emotions” in Ukraine, Russia and Europe.
Before launching its 2022 invasion, Moscow had demanded that Nato roll back troops from eastern Europe and has throughout the war aired its grievances towards the West.
Russia has, for the first time, included in its delegation a diplomat -- Sergei Ryabkov -- who issued an ultimatum to the West on re-writing European security before Moscow launched the war.
The head of Moscow’s delegation, President Vladimir Putin’s nationalistic aide Vladimir Medinsky, said he hoped Moscow’s “bigger and more professional” team will “enable us to move forwards on the path towards peace.”
A source in the Russian team earlier said that “the Ukrainian settlement, whilst a critically important issue, is merely one item on the agenda” of the talks.
The main objective was “the creation of a comprehensive and indivisible security architecture for the entire continent,” it added.
Nato’s general in Europe, Alexus Grynkewich, is also taking part in the talks.
In a joint statement, the Europeans, Ukraine, US and Nato said they held a meeting before meeting Russia, reaffirming their “shared commitment to a strong post-war European security architecture.”
Europe has been alarmed by Trump’s plans and the EU said on the eve of the talks that “meaningful” security discussions can only take place after a ceasefire in Ukraine.
Putin has refused broader ceasefires and face-to-face talks with Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky, vowing his troops will press on to seize more land in Ukraine.
Kyiv’s top negotiator Umerov said Ukraine’s priority in the talks remained securing a ceasefire.
“Our people are waiting to end this war,” he said.
Ukraine has resisted Russia’s invasion at a huge human cost, with thousands of civilians killed and millions forced to flee their homes.
“We hope that we will achieve a lasting peace for Ukraine,” Umerov said, saying Kyiv wanted to discuss “security guarantees.”
There is huge distrust in Ukraine towards Trump’s aims, with the US leader appearing to veer towards Moscow this year, signing a diesel deal with Putin and criticizing Zelensky.
Trump hinted ahead of the talks that Ukraine might have to give up land, saying: “They’re going to end up with a little bit different shape, Ukraine.”
Russia occupies large swathes of Ukraine but, while its troops have inched westwards, they have not been able to seize the whole of the Donetsk region.
Moscow demands Kyiv surrender the parts of the region it still controls, vowing it will otherwise press on with its offensive.
Russia pummeled Ukraine in the run-up to the talks and carried out one of its deadliest strikes yet -- with Kyiv saying 55 people were killed in a frontline village as they queued for humanitarian aid.
Zelensky said the intensified strikes were part of Moscow’s strategy of “putting pressure on Ukraine’s position” at the negotiations.
The Ukrainian military said on Tuesday that Russia had fired 162 drones and one ballistic missile overnight.
Kushner and Witkoff are bringing the enemy sides together for the first time since February, when negotiations took place in Geneva.
Russia and Ukraine have held several rounds of failed talks during almost five years of war and hopes for peace are low.
“We don’t have any particular expectations,” a senior Ukrainian official in Kyiv told AFP.

item.title: French students block dozens of schools
item.description:
French students blocked the entrances to dozens of high schools on Tuesday, the education ministry said, as they kept up protests for better learning conditions.
Student protests across France since September have spiraled into larger cost-of-living demonstrations in recent weeks, some marked by fringe violence and accusations of police brutality.
The unrest comes ahead of elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron next year.
With the European Union’s second-largest economy under pressure to rein in debt, the government has limited scope to appease protesters through additional spending.
Forty-nine of the country’s 3,700 high schools for 15 to 18-year-olds were blockaded on Tuesday morning, the ministry said. Authorities expected several thousand school and university students at a Paris protest on Tuesday afternoon.
“Now is the time to step up the mobilization by continuing to put pressure on the government,” student and teacher unions said in a joint statement released Monday.
Student association leader Ryad Rani said it was essential to keep up the pressure.
“We’re not just fighting for ourselves. We’re fighting for teachers, for their working conditions,” he said.
The government has announced measures including the gradual replacement of an online selection platform to access higher education, as well as financial means for some of the worst-off schools.
But students say this is not enough.
Unions are not happy either, with one leader saying on Monday that a government pledge to increase to the minimum wage by 0.6% on top of a standard adjustment for inflation was “crumbs.”
They have called for a new day of strikes and protest on November 17.
Around 575,000 people demonstrated across the country during cost-of-living strikes and protests last Thursday, according to authorities. Unions put the number at 1.5 million.

item.title: Trump sees 'positive momentum' on Iran after Qatar PM talks
item.description:
US President Donald Trump said on Monday there was momentum toward ending the war with Iran, as he declared that the country "militarily is effectively over," but kept open the possibility of new strikes.
Trump met at the White House with Qatar Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani -- a key mediator in the Iran war. It was his first meeting with a foreign leader since his party's massive losses in the midterm elections.
Trump later posted on Truth Social that the two leaders had "an excellent conversation" and that "much was discussed with respect to the Islamic Republic of Iran."
In the weeks leading up to the midterms, there was widespread speculation that US strikes against Iran would resume soon after.
However, Trump has talked down resuming the conflict while leaving the door open to further strikes -- a position he reiterated Monday at a White House press briefing.
"Iran, militarily, is effectively over. We're just keeping it the status quo," Trump told reporters. "But if we do have to go back in, we are locked and loaded, and ready to go."
In his social post on Monday, Trump said that he believed further strikes were "quite unlikely" given that key US allies in the Gulf "would prefer the status quo."
"We are seeing positive momentum toward an end to this Conflict, and will ensure that America's interests are at all times protected," Trump said.
Iranian officials meanwhile expressed defiance at the continued pressure from Washington.
The Islamic republic's top security chief, Mohsen Rezai, wrote on X late Monday that the US "flails like a desperate gambler," telling Washington to "fold your hand. Stop manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks."
Earlier, Tehran's top negotiator Mahammad Bagher Ghalibaf claimed on X that Israel was pushing the US deeper into conflict, adding that "unless Washington drops the 'Israel First' mindset, America and its allies are headed straight for a dark age."
On the ground in Iran, strikes -- which have not been publicly acknowledged by the US military -- are continuing, according to Iranian authorities.
The island of Qeshm, located in the Strait of Hormuz, was targeted overnight from Sunday to Monday, the provincial deputy governor stated on state television.
Trump has acknowledged that the highly unpopular war with Iran was at least partially responsible for the Republicans' defeat, not least because it has contributed to rising prices in the US economy.
