item.title: Consumers Forum: Essential goods prices rise by 4.39% in October
item.description:
Prices of essential commodities across the country increased by an average of 4.39% in October, driven largely by a sharp hike in fish and spice prices, according to findings by the Consumers Forum (CF).
Data compiled by the organization across various markets in Dhaka—including Karwan Bazar, Rampura, Meradia, Aftabnagar's Bhuiyan Bazar, and several super shops—showed that prices of 15 key categories of goods rose during the month.
Fish prices recorded the highest surge, jumping by an average of 11.72%.
Prices of spices, including cloves, cardamom, cinnamon, and cumin, rose by 10.30%, while onions, garlic, and ginger saw a 7.79% increase.
Other notable price hikes included fuel oil (6.02%), sugar (4.93%), edible oil and dalda (4.80%), flour and maida (3.25%), rice (2.62%), eggs (1.42%), meat (0.38%), and tea (0.14%).
Conversely, prices of seven essential items, including salt, dairy products, toothpaste, biscuits, 11 major brands of medicines, and stationery items, remained stable.
Meanwhile, prices dropped for two categories: vegetables fell by 3.12% and gold and silver by 4.77%.
Field reports from different parts of the vegetable supply hub, including Jessore, Bogra, and Rangpur, indicated that winter vegetables have begun arriving in local wholesale markets, though producers are struggling to recover their production costs.
While cauliflower and cabbage sold for Tk6–12, radishes for Tk6–8, gourds for Tk8–10, and plantains for Tk5–8 per 4-piece (hali) locally in regions like Bogra and Rangpur, they were retailed at much higher prices in Dhaka, with cauliflowers and cabbages fetching around Tk50, papayas and radishes Tk30, gourds Tk60, and plantains Tk40–50 per hali.
According to the Consumers Forum, essential commodity prices had already risen by 3.13% in September, bringing the cumulative two-month increase to 7.52%.
In a press release issued Sunday by CF General Secretary Emdad Hossain Malek, the organization emphasized that merely raising wages is insufficient.
It called on authorities to keep essential living expenses—including urban house and shop rents, education, and healthcare—within the purchasing power of middle and lower-middle-income groups.
The forum urged strict administrative and legal actions to curb excessive profit-seeking by unscrupulous traders and safeguard public welfare.

item.title: DSCC administrator urges capacity-based disaster response
item.description:
Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) Administrator Bir Muktijoddha Md Abdus Salam has called for coordinated efforts among the Fire Service, police, Red Crescent and other agencies to ensure public safety during emergencies.
He made the call while chairing the fifth meeting of the DSCC Disaster Management Committee at Nagar Bhaban on Monday afternoon, said a press release.
Abdus Salam said disaster preparedness must reflect the rescue equipment and operational capabilities of each agency, rather than remain limited to paper-based responsibility sharing.
Highlighting the unplanned development of much of Dhaka South, he stressed the need for joint efforts, regular drills and public awareness programs to reduce risks from fires, building collapses and earthquakes.
Referring to the recent fire at Moulvibazar in Old Dhaka, he said narrow roads, water shortages and roadside shops and vendors had hampered firefighters' access to the scene.
He said high-rise buildings and commercial establishments must have basic firefighting equipment and fire hydrants. He also called for underground installation of overhead cables and the preservation of ponds and water bodies, including those in Dholaikhal, to ensure adequate water for firefighting.
The meeting, attended by 57 representatives of government and private organizations, NGOs, and social organizations, also discussed agencies' responsibilities before, during, and after disasters.

item.title: Home minister vows strict action against attempts to create unrest
item.description:
Police will take legal action and deal firmly with those behind attacks on buses and establishments amid recent cocktail explosions and sporadic unrest in different parts of the capital, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has said.
"We have noticed that the fallen forces occasionally attack buses and establishments to create instability. Police will take legal action and deal with them firmly," he told reporters in front of the Ministry of Home Affairs on Monday.
Asked who was behind the unrest, the home minister said: "Whoever they are, they are miscreants."
Asked about the nationwide strike called by the Awami League, whose activities have been banned and its banned student wing, Bangladesh Chhatra League, he responded: "Is that so? Then you will see how the strike takes place."
At least eight buses have been set on fire and more than 50 crude bomb explosions have been reported at different locations in the capital over the past few days.

item.title: Delhi mission forwards Hasina's passport, NID request to Dhaka
item.description:
The Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi has received an email from Matrix Chambers, a London-based law firm, requesting a new passport and national identity card (NID) for ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, reports Prothom Alo.
However, diplomatic sources in Dhaka said it was not possible to verify whether the request had actually come from Sheikh Hasina. The email contained no documents or proof of authorization from her, which would typically be required when an organization submits an application on someone else's behalf.
A diplomatic source in New Delhi confirmed to Prothom Alo that the High Commission received the email on Monday morning. The mission subsequently contacted the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Dhaka for guidance on how to proceed.
Sources at the ministry also confirmed receipt of the information from the High Commission.
According to sources familiar with the communication, a lawyer from Matrix Chambers stated at the beginning of the email that the firm was acting on behalf of Sheikh Hasina. The email outlined several points and requested the issuance of a new passport and NID card.
It also referred to reports that the interim government and other authorities had revoked Hasina's existing Bangladeshi passport and NID.
The Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi was asked to take the necessary steps to issue her new documents.
Earlier, Reuters reported, citing a letter it had obtained, that Sheikh Hasina had requested a new passport and NID card to facilitate her return to Bangladesh. The request was reportedly submitted to the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi.

item.title: Duchess of Edinburgh meets Zubaida Rahman
item.description:
The Duchess of Edinburgh, Sophie, met Dr Zubaida Rahman, wife of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, in Dhaka on Monday to discuss shared priorities in promoting the welfare, protection and empowerment of women and girls.
The meeting took place at the Crowne Plaza hotel shortly after the Duchess arrived in Bangladesh. State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam was also present, according to the BNP media cell.
The Duchess is visiting Bangladesh from November 9 to 11 at the invitation of the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO).
During her visit, she is scheduled to meet representatives of different communities and organisations to highlight the breadth of the UK-Bangladesh partnership and areas of cooperation.
She will also visit Cox’s Bazar to see humanitarian programmes and meet organisations working to support Rohingya refugees sheltering in Bangladesh.

item.title: Bus overturns in Lakshmipur, killing 3, injuring 15
item.description:
Three people, including a woman, were killed and at least 15 others injured when a passenger bus overturned in the Charchamita area of Chandraganj, Lakshmipur, on Monday, reports Bangla Tribune.
The accident occurred around 11:30am on the Lakshmipur-Noakhali highway.
The victims were two men and a woman. Two of them have been identified as Mansura Begum and Babul Hossain.
Adel Akbar, officer-in-charge of Chandraganj Highway Police Station, confirmed the deaths and injuries. He said the injured were rescued and taken to Lakshmipur Sadar Hospital.
Among the injured were Nazim Uddin, Rashed, Basudev, Siddiqur Rahman, Palash Uddin and Khorshed.
An elderly couple, Abdur Rahman and his wife, Sajeda Begum, were also injured. They suffered injuries to their heads, arms and other parts of their bodies and were admitted to the hospital after receiving initial treatment.
Abdur Rahman said they were travelling from Begumganj towards Lakshmipur when the accident occurred. He alleged that the bus driver was driving recklessly and failed to slow down despite passengers asking him to do so. The bus eventually overturned in the Charchamita area.
Highway police and local sources said the bus, operated by Anand Paribahan under Nafis Enterprise, lost control and overturned. Three passengers died on the spot and at least 15 others were injured. The wrecked bus was later removed from the road.
Dr Zahurul Islam Roni, the physician on duty at Lakshmipur Sadar Hospital, said three people were brought to the hospital dead, while at least 15 injured passengers received treatment. Several of them were referred to hospitals in Noakhali and Dhaka for advanced treatment.

item.title: Auto-rickshaw drivers block road in front of Press Club over 12-point demand
item.description:
Battery-run auto-rickshaw drivers blocked the road in front of the National Press Club in Dhaka on Monday, pressing home their 12-point demand.
They blocked the road around 12pm after gathering in front of the Press Club in processions from different parts of the capital.
The drivers also suspended auto-rickshaw services across the city as part of the program.
Mahbub, an auto-rickshaw driver, said: “We are holding this programme to press our 12-point demands.”
Meanwhile, law enforcement agencies remained on alert around the protesters.
Deputy Commissioner of Police (Ramna Division) Sheikh Zahidul Islam said additional police personnel had been deployed to prevent any disorder.
“We are keeping a close watch on the situation,” he said.

item.title: Public university admission tests to begin in February
item.description:
First-year admission tests at public universities for the 2026-27 academic session are expected to begin in February next year, with applications opening in January.
University Grants Commission (UGC) Chairman Professor Dr Mamun Ahmed announced the plan at a press briefing on Monday following a meeting with public university vice-chancellors at the UGC headquarters.
He said universities had agreed to coordinate their admission test schedules to avoid clashes and allow students to sit for tests at multiple institutions.
The decision comes as the number of students who passed this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations fell to slightly over 600,000, down from more than 700,000 last year.
Mamun said answer scripts were being re-evaluated and supplementary examinations arranged for students who failed to achieve their expected results. The government aims to publish the results of both by December 31.
Students who pass the re-evaluation or supplementary examinations will also be eligible for university admission tests, he added.
The UGC chairman said vice-chancellors had been asked to consider Ramadan when setting admission test dates. Universities that have already announced their schedules have also been urged to reconsider them to avoid clashes.
The meeting also discussed forming a central coordination committee comprising representatives from the UGC, the Ministry of Education and universities to oversee admission schedules throughout the year.
On admission test formats, Mamun said universities would retain the multiple-choice question (MCQ) system for the current academic session. However, they are considering introducing subject-based and analytical questions alongside MCQs from the next session to assess students' subject knowledge, analytical skills and problem-solving abilities.
Vice-chancellors were also asked to consider GPA requirements in determining admission test eligibility, taking into account this year's HSC results and available seats.
Mamun said universities had been urged to ensure that the delayed admission tests did not disrupt regular academic activities, adding that the UGC would provide necessary support.
Bangladesh currently has around 180 public and private universities. Public universities offer approximately 63,000 first-year seats, while institutions affiliated with the National University, Islamic Arabic University and other public universities have more than one million seats combined. Private universities offer more than 400,000 seats.
He stressed that the coordination initiative would respect university autonomy, with institutions retaining authority over their admission processes under their respective laws and regulations.

item.title: Chittagong couple lose both sons to measles, dengue
item.description:
A Chittagong couple have lost both their sons to measles and dengue within two days, with their 10-month-old younger child dying late Sunday night, following the death of his 10-year-old brother on Friday.
The two children, Nur Mohammad Arafat and Mohammad Abu Bakkar, had been undergoing treatment at Chittagong Maa-O-Shishu Hospital.
Overcome with grief after losing his younger son, Mohammad Kabir said in a tearful voice: “I couldn't save my boy.”
Abu Bakkar died at 1:10am on Monday while undergoing treatment at the hospital. His elder brother, Arafat, died at the same hospital on Friday morning.
Professor Didarul Alam, head of the hospital's Paediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU), confirmed Abu Bakkar's death, saying the child had succumbed to measles and dengue.
After losing his elder son, Kabir had pinned his remaining hopes on Abu Bakkar. But that hope was also shattered. The younger child was placed on life support on Saturday after his condition deteriorated. On Sunday, doctors informed the family that his condition was critical. Despite the warning, Kabir continued to hope that his son would survive.
Arafat was a Class III student at Hillview Public School in the Panchlaish area of Chittagong city. Around 15-20 days ago, he developed a fever, vomiting and a cough. He was initially treated at Southern Hospital and later at Imperial Hospital. As his condition worsened, he was admitted to an intensive care unit before being transferred to Chittagong Maa-O-Shishu Hospital.
According to his father, Arafat was suffering from measles, dengue and pneumonia, with complications affecting his lungs and liver. He last spoke to his father on Thursday night. When his condition deteriorated on Friday morning, doctors asked Kabir to come to the hospital. However, Arafat died before his father could reach him. He was buried that evening at a graveyard in the city's Momenbagh area.
After burying his elder son, Kabir stayed at the hospital as Abu Bakkar continued to receive treatment. The younger child was placed on life support on Saturday as his condition worsened, but doctors could not save him.
Kabir lived with his wife, Amena Begum, and their two sons in a rented house in the Hillview area of Chittagong city. The 31-year-old works in cargo handling for a private company, earning around Tk20,000 a month, of which Tk6,000 goes towards rent. Despite his modest income, he had many dreams for his two children.
Whenever he returned home from work, his sons would rush to greet him. Now, he dreads returning to the house filled with memories of them.
“When I came home from work, my two boys would run into my arms. I had so many dreams, so many plans. Every corner of our small home holds memories of them. How can I go back there? How can I live there?” he said.
Kabir spent all his savings trying to save his children. He sought help from colleagues, neighbours and relatives and even took on debt to cover their medical expenses. Despite his efforts, he lost both sons.
Amena is also devastated. Kabir said her physical and mental health had deteriorated following Arafat's death. Overcome with grief, she repeatedly lost consciousness and could not eat properly. As a result, she had to remain at home while Abu Bakkar was receiving treatment.
With both children gone, Kabir and Amena's home is now without the laughter and presence of their two boys. The rooms that once echoed with their play and footsteps are filled only with memories. After days of struggling to save their sons, the grieving parents are left to mourn the loss of both children.

item.title: PM Tarique to leave for Türkiye Tuesday to attend COP31 summit
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will leave Dhaka on Tuesday for an official visit to Türkiye to attend the World Leaders’ Summit of COP31, scheduled to be held in Antalya on November 11-12.
The prime minister is scheduled to address a plenary session on November 12 and hold several bilateral meetings with world leaders on the sidelines of the summit.
Newly appointed Foreign Secretary Salahuddin Noman Chowdhury briefed reporters about the visit at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Sunday.
Bangladesh is looking to arrange bilateral meetings with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, the Australian prime minister, the president of Uzbekistan and the British foreign secretary.
Additional Foreign Secretary (Public Diplomacy and Other Priority Matters) AKM Shahidul Karim and senior ministry officials were also present.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam recently said Bangladesh would urge developed countries to provide climate finance in the form of grants rather than loans and take responsibility for their contribution to global carbon emissions at the upcoming COP31.
COP, officially known as the Conference of the Parties, is the annual United Nations climate summit.
Bangladesh will highlight its achievements in climate resilience and share its experience in addressing the impacts of climate change across South Asia and the wider Asian region.
At the same time, the country will draw attention to the support it needs to tackle future climate challenges, particularly the importance of ensuring that climate finance comes in the form of grants rather than loans.
Bangladesh will also press major carbon-emitting countries to take responsibility for their emissions and ensure accountability in global climate negotiations.
"Although Bangladesh's contribution to global carbon emissions is almost negligible, we are ultimately among those suffering the consequences," Shama Obaed said recently.
The government will also showcase the initiatives taken by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman over the past six months to address climate change and improve the environment.
These include canal excavation, tree plantation drives and a stronger focus on solar power and renewable energy, all of which contribute to climate change mitigation and environmental protection.
An inter-ministerial coordination meeting chaired by State Minister Shama last month reviewed Bangladesh's preparations for the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31).
The meeting discussed various aspects of the preparations, including the Prime Minister's participation in the high-level segment of the summit.
It also reviewed Bangladesh's priorities and concerns, possible bilateral engagements and seminars to be organised at the country's pavilions in the Blue and Green Zones on the sidelines of COP31.

item.title: Madrasa teacher held over burning 9-year-old student
item.description:
Police have arrested a madrasa teacher in Tongi, Gazipur, for allegedly burning a nine-year-old student with a hot iron.
The accused, Rabbi Hossain, 25, was detained late Sunday and later shown arrested in a case filed over a written complaint by the child's mother.
Rabbi teaches at Miftahul Madrasa in the Cherag Ali area of Tongi. He is a resident of Hossainpur Upazila in Kishoreganj.
According to the complaint, the teacher allegedly pressed a hot iron against the boy's lower back on Wednesday afternoon.
The next day, when the mother went to the madrasa to bring her son home, the child told her about the alleged abuse. She subsequently lodged a written complaint with Tongi East Police Station.
Officer-in-Charge of the police station, Maksudul Alam, said the teacher had initially admitted to the incident during questioning.
He said a case was filed based on the mother's complaint and the teacher was shown arrested. He was scheduled to be produced before a court on Monday.

item.title: Two buses set on fire on Dhaka-Aricha highway
item.description:
Miscreants set fire to two parked buses at separate locations along the Dhaka-Aricha highway in Savar late Sunday night.
One of the buses belonged to Itihas Paribahan, while the other was used to transport garment workers.
Jahangir Alam, a senior station officer at Savar Fire Service, confirmed the incidents on Monday morning.
According to the Fire Service, the first incident occurred at Genda bus stand, where a bus used to transport garment workers was parked. Miscreants allegedly set the vehicle on fire and fled the scene. Firefighters later arrived and brought the blaze under control.
In a separate incident, around 4am, a passenger bus operated by Itihas Paribahan caught fire in front of a Tata servicing centre near Baliarpur bus stand along the same highway. Firefighters responded to the scene and extinguished the blaze.
Jahangir Alam said the two incidents involved a worker-transport bus in Genda and an Itihas Paribahan passenger bus in Baliarpur.
He added that preliminary assessments suggested both buses had been deliberately set on fire as acts of sabotage.

item.title: 34 platoons of BGB deployed in industrial areas of Dhaka, Gazipur, Narayanganj
item.description:
A total of 34 platoons of the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) have been deployed in key industrial areas of Dhaka, Gazipur and Narayanganj to ensure security, maintain law and order and prevent any untoward incidents amid ongoing worker unrest.
The BGB Media Department disclosed the information on Monday.
The deployed personnel are performing duties at various key locations, including Savar, Ashulia and Mirpur in Dhaka; Shibu Market, Jalkuri, BSCIC Industrial Estate, Chashara, Kanchpur and Shimrail in Narayanganj; and Chandra, Kaliakair, Palli Bidyut, Mouchak, Ambag Kata, Naojor, Bhogra Bypass, Gacha and Salna in Gazipur.
The BGB headquarters' monitoring cell is continuing technology-based surveillance to closely monitor the overall situation in industrial areas and coordinate the activities of personnel deployed on the ground.
Live footage obtained through drones, body-worn cameras and improvised devices is being monitored round the clock.
BGB personnel are performing their duties on high alert in coordination with the local administration and police.
The force is also maintaining necessary preparations and operations to address any unforeseen situation and maintain peace and order in industrial areas.

Nvidia announces probe into Huang amid reports China spied on him
item.description:
Chip giant Nvidia's board announced Sunday it opened a probe into Chief Executive and co-founder Jensen Huang after he acknowledged an affair with a woman US officials say was working for Chinese intelligence.
Late last month, The New York Times reported that US intelligence officials concluded that the woman, a Chinese executive linked to a Singapore-based data center company called Megaspeed, had been funnelling information to Beijing.
The executive, Alice Huang -- also known as Huang Le, and no relation to 63-year-old Taiwanese-born Jensen Huang -- developed a close relationship with the Nvidia boss, the Times said.
In a message to company employees released Sunday, Huang acknowledged having an affair and apologized to both his family and company staff.
"I was unfaithful to my wife," he said. "My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."
Asked about the report Sunday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he couldn't comment, saying it was an "internal corporate matter."
Jensen Huang is a key figure in the artificial intelligence revolution and close to President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly spoken out against regulating the industry so as not to let China gain the upper hand in the AI race.
The Times said Huang's relationship with the other Huang could have given her insights into Trump's thinking around AI. The issue of AI is likely to arise during Trump's planned talks with President Xi Jinping later this month at a summit in China.
Nvidia said in a statement it opened an independent probe "in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort." It did not name a country.
The statement added: "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information."
The Chinese government has dismissed the Times report as "groundless speculation."
China is in a race for tech dominance with the United States, which restricts the export to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips.
Nvidia, a global leader in producing chips used to train and run AI models, is one of the world's most valuable companies.
Megaspeed was under scrutiny for possibly steering Nvidia AI chips to China, the Times report said, citing unnamed sources briefed on the matter.
Trump was briefed on the intelligence findings about Huang's relationship with the businesswoman roughly a year ago and chose not to act on the information, the Times report said.
Technology analyst Dan Ives, with the investment bank Yorkville Ives, said word of the probe is "a black eye moment" for Jensen Huang.
Ives predicted it will at the very least spark multiple congressional inquiries and "create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons."
In the near-term Huang is expected to keep his job but risks being removed as Nvidia's CEO depending on the board's probe, Ives said in a statement.
"This will add risk to the stock as he is so important to the Nvidia story and strategy globally," he said. "This will also increase major scrutiny regarding selling chips to China, which remains a key battleground issue in DC."

item.title: Inter beat Como to close in on Serie A leaders Lazio
item.description:
Inter Milan claimed a statement 2-0 win over Como on Sunday to move just one point behind Serie A leaders Lazio, who were held to a 1-1 draw at Napoli.
Francesco Pio Esposito and Marcus Thuram struck in the opening 20 minutes as Inter ended a six-match winning run from Como that included the biggest away win in Champions League history, Wednesday's 9-1 demolition of French side Lens.
Inter, who suffered their first league defeat of the season to rivals AC Milan a week ago, jumped back into second as a thrilling title race heats up, with two points separating Lazio from third-placed Roma.
"Today we played well in every aspect. We put pressure on their build-up and accepted that they could cause us problems," said Inter coach Cristian Chivu.
"We counter-attacked with ferocity and were clinical in front of goal. I applaud my players for a performance of maturity and quality."
Cesc Fabregas' Como were outclassed in defeat at San Siro, allowing Milan to leapfrog them into fourth on 24 points after Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic struck in a 2-1 win over Genoa.
Inter made a fast start as they looked to put the memory of last weekend's Milan derby defeat behind them, Esposito tapping in an inviting Djed Spence cross after 12 minutes.
They soon made it two when a poor clearance dropped invitingly into Thuram's path in the box and the France international lashed a shot past Robert Sanchez.
Como mustered little in response in an uncharacteristically muted display as Federico Dimarco and Thuram threatened a third with efforts in the second half, before Nico Paz clipped the crossbar late on.
Leaders Lazio dropped points for just the second time this season at struggling Napoli as Davide Frattesi's opener was cancelled out by an Alfonso Pedraza own goal.
Napoli were under pressure to deliver a result after defeats by Juventus and Porto saw the squad sent into a training retreat in a bid to revive their flagging form.
But they could only claim a point against Gennaro Gattuso's unbeaten outfit, whose remarkable form continued as they remained 14 points ahead of 10th-placed Napoli.
"We must keep going, everything's not lost even if we are behind in the standings," Napoli coach Massimiliano Allegri said.
Milan finished a mixed week on a high as a second Serie A win on the bounce took them into the top four.
Ruben Amorim's side impressed with their 3-1 Milan derby win last weekend, but inconsistency reared its head again with a 2-0 Europa League loss at home to Ferencvaros on Thursday.
Amorim was left furious by his side's performance in that game but saw a much-improved start from his players at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris.
Cisse swept in the opener after 13 minutes before Pulisic doubled their lead six minutes later, and Mikael Ellertsson's late strike for Genoa proved no more than a consolation.
Juventus lost more ground as they twice fought back to claim a 2-2 draw with Fiorentina in Florence.
The result left Luciano Spalletti's side seventh with 18 points, while Fiorentina moved two points clear of the relegation zone on nine points.
Mateo Pellegrino headed Fiorentina in front from a corner after just four minutes, but Juventus levelled when Randal Kolo Muani cut in from the right wing and teed up strike partner Nick Woltemade for his first Serie A goal.
Alieu Njie restored the hosts' lead early in the second half with his third goal in three games after a goalmouth scramble, but Juve responded when some uncertain goalkeeping from David de Gea allowed Gleison Bremer to head a corner into an unguarded net.
Guglielmo Vicario produced two big saves in the dying minutes as Fiorentina tried in vain to take the lead for a third time.
Atalanta ended a six-match winless run in all competitions by beating Monza 1-0 thanks to a Nikola Krstovic strike.

item.title: Lopez double earns Liga leaders Barca win at Atletico
item.description:
Fermin Lopez struck twice to help Barcelona come from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 on Sunday and move three points clear at the top of La Liga.
The Spanish champions lead second place Real Madrid, who beat Valencia 3-0 on Saturday, by three points with Atletico third and a further two points off the pace.
Giuliano Simeone fired Atletico ahead in a high-octane start, before Lopez pulled Barca level shortly before the interval at the Metropolitano stadium.
The 23-year-old Spain international netted the winner after 66 minutes when Lamine Yamal slipped him in, helping Barca triumph despite not being at their best.
Last season Atletico defeated Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals and also in the Copa del Rey, but the Catalans earned some measure of revenge here.
"Coming off last season, when they beat us... we knew what they were going to offer -- a very difficult game," Lopez told Movistar.
"It got tricky for us in the first half with their goal, but I think we knew how to come back and we had a great match."
After criticism following defeats by Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid in recent weeks, Flick's side proved they can handle themselves in big matches.
"We have the quality to win these matches... I totally believe in the team," Flick told reporters.
"In the second half especially we did a great job today, it's not easy to win here."
Atletico coach Diego Simeone said his team performed well despite the result.
"I have nothing to complain about, we played the match we wanted to play," he told reporters.
"I'm leaving here knowing that we are a work in progress, that we still have things to improve, and that obviously we have players who still need to keep growing."
The match started at a fast pace and both teams hit the woodwork in the opening stages.
Alvarez, who tried and failed to force a move from Atletico to Barca in the summer, rounded goalkeeper Joan Garcia but could not finish off the chance as the defence blocked his route to goal.
From the resulting corner Atletico defender Marc Pubill headed against the crossbar with Garcia beaten.
At the other end Pedri crashed a strike against the woodwork after being fed by Barca's teenage star Lamine Yamal.
Atletico took the lead in the 10th minute, slicing Barca's defence open. Alvarez crossed for Giuliano Simeone to turn home from close range.
Alvarez was denied by Garcia as Atletico looked for a second and Barca struggled to click into their top gears.
Despite their struggles they went in level at the break, with a goal out of nowhere.
Lopez's path to the box was blocked but the ball bounced loose to the midfielder and he quickly smashed a strike past Jan Oblak.
Early in the second half Alvarez lobbed a good chance over the crossbar when running in on goal.
"He's a great player, we love him... we need the best version of Julian Alvarez, without him we won't get to where we want to be," said Diego Simeone.
The forward came to rue the miss when Barcelona took the lead.
Yamal played a clever pass through Atletico's defence and Lopez kept his cool to beat Oblak. It was his seventh league goal in 11 top flight appearances this season.
Barcelona kept Atletico at bay well in the final stages to take three points home from the capital before the international break.
Atletico captain Koke said his team would not let the defeat, their first in La Liga since September 5, upset them too much.
"I think the team had a really great first half. We had chances to kill off the game and we didn't take them," said Koke.
Earlier on fourth-place Real Betis earned a 2-0 win at Elche, while Real Sociedad, fifth, defeated Rayo Vallecano 1-0.
Villarreal beat Getafe 2-0 to move eighth and Celta Vigo and Levante shared a goalless draw.

item.title: Alcaraz downs Shelton to win Paris Masters for first time
item.description:
Carlos Alcaraz gained a measure of revenge on Ben Shelton on Sunday as the seven-time Grand Slam champion beat the American 7-6 (7/5), 7-5 to win the Paris Masters for the first time.
In defeating the man who ended his US Open title defence earlier this season, the 23-year-old claimed the ninth 1000-level title of his career.
Unlike their five-set quarter-final epic in New York two months ago, the clash in Paris lasted just under two hours.
"For me it's really special that finally I just got to play great tennis," Alcaraz told reporters. "I went far in the tournament, lifting the trophy at the end.
"I would say this week I took a step forward mentally. I had a lot of really tough moments.
"I'm just really happy that I controlled my emotions, controlled my thoughts every moment, every single match," he added in reference to his quarter-final win against Taylor Fritz in which he saved two match points.
Coming into Paris on the back of winning the 500-level title in Vienna, Alcaraz has won his last nine matches.
"Probably these two last weeks have been the best I've played since my comeback," Alcaraz added of his return from a wrist injury that caused him to miss the French Open and Wimbledon.
Ahead of the ATP Finals, which run November 15-22 in Turin, world number three Alcaraz now holds five tour-level titles this year -- only the injured Jannik Sinner has more with six.
In Italy, he will next be seeking a first coronation at the season-ending Finals.
For world number four Shelton, it was a first defeat in a Masters final after winning his two previous appearances in showpiece matches at that level -- both coming in the last two editions of the Canadian Open.
An entertaining first set which drew a multitude of admiring gasps from the crowd went the distance despite both players enjoying some success on the other's serve.
In the tie-break, a Shelton error at 4-4 followed by a leaping backhand smash by Alcaraz brought up two set points.
The first came and went when Alcaraz thundered the ball into the top of the net cord and the expectant arena froze in time as it rose and fell in seeming slow motion, only to land on the Spaniard's side of the court.
Alcaraz was not to be denied a second time, however, as Shelton overcooked a forehand on the next point to cede the opener.
At 2-2 in the second set, Shelton let out a bellow of frustration after missing a groundstroke at 15-30 on Alcaraz's serve, but the American could smile at the end of the game as a double fault and missed forehand produced the first break of the match.
Alcaraz had said after booking his spot in the final that his reflexes would need to be "ten out of ten" when facing Shelton's serve and they were just that three games later as he levelled the set at four-all.
A deft exchange of angled drop shots ended by an Alcaraz winner down the line brought the Spaniard's finger to his ear and the crowd again to their feet as Shelton suddenly found himself serving to keep the final alive.
He did so at the first time of asking but when required to serve again to force a breaker, Shelton cracked as Alcaraz again pounced to seal the title with a flicked backhand winner.
"It's all about the little details. The difference in our match in the US Open was the little details, and same here," 24-year-old Shelton said.
"I've learned so much, and it's the position that I want to be in.
"Playing in the US Open final against (Alexander) Zverev, playing the finals here against Carlos, now going to Turin and get to line up against the eight best players in the world."
After winning two French Opens and now the Paris Masters, former world number one Alcaraz is undefeated in title matches in the city, excluding the Olympic Games which do not carry ranking points.
In the earlier doubles final, French pair Quentin Halys and Pierre-Hugues Herbert upset second seeds Neal Skupski and Christian Harrison as the wildcards triumphed 7-6 (7/3), 6-7 (4/7), 10-8.

item.title: Man Utd rescue Villa draw with incredible fightback, Chelsea stunned
item.description:
Manchester United rescued an incredible 4-4 draw against Aston Villa as two stoppage-time goals gave Michael Carrick renewed hope of avoiding the sack, while Chelsea suffered a shock 1-0 loss at Sunderland on Sunday.
United boss Carrick was seconds away from heading into the international break on the back of another devastating defeat that would surely have led to his dismissal.
But Carrick's side struck twice in the six minutes of additional time through Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu to leave their manager's future still uncertain.
United are in the relegation zone and have not won in their last eight Premier League matches, so it is far from sure that Carrick will survive the axe.
He had earned a stay of execution when United's hierarchy allowed him to remain in charge despite last weekend's loss at Chelsea.
United responded by ending a nine-match winless run in all competitions as they came from two goals down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday.
But United, who have only three wins in 15 games this season, were back in turmoil when they fell 2-0 down against Villa in the first four minutes at Old Trafford.
Alysson struck in the first minute with a shot that squirmed under United keeper Senne Lammens.
Nicolas Jackson slotted in the second three minutes later after a weak save from Lammens pushed the ball into his path.
Bruno Fernandes got one back with a 16th-minute penalty after Boubacar Kamara fouled Matheus Cunha before former Villa midfielder Youri Tielemans slammed in United's 44th-minute equaliser.
Villa's John McGinn converted a 48th-minute penalty following Diogo Dalot's clumsy challenge on Alysson.
Leon Goretzka poked in Villa's fourth from close-range after United's Leny Yoro headed against his own crossbar in the 53rd minute.
Yet Zirkzee's stoppage-time finish gave United hope and Dorgu headed their dramatic equaliser in the final seconds after a weak punch from Villa keeper Zion Suzuki.
Carrick wore a bewildered look on his face as he walked down the tunnel towards an uncertain future, with United next in action at Liverpool on November 22.
Chelsea arrived at the Stadium of Light hoping to bolster their bid to qualify for the Champions League via a top-four finish.
Instead, they departed red-faced after an embarrassing loss to third-bottom Sunderland, who celebrated a league victory for only the second time this season.
Fifth-placed Chelsea have already been beaten four times in 10 league matches under former Real Madrid boss Xabi Alonso.
Chelsea were rocked in the 36th minute when Enzo Le Fee converted a penalty after Brian Brobbey was up-ended by Levi Colwill.
"We were not creating enough chances in the final third against the low block. We were not controlling and sustaining the attack there," Alonso said.
Liverpool got back on track with a 3-1 win at lowly Crystal Palace.
The Reds had been beaten by Arsenal and Fenerbahce before arriving in south London, sparking pointed questions about Andoni Iraola in the former Bournemouth manager's first season in charge.
But Alexis Mac Allister headed Liverpool in front from Dominik Szoboszlai's cross after 40 minutes.
Florian Wirtz bagged Liverpool's second with a composed finish from Bradley Barcola's cross in the 54th minute.
Alexander Isak finished off Wirtz's pass in the 89th minute to wrap up fourth-placed Liverpool's much-needed victory after a two-game losing streak.
"It was an important win for us going into the international break after the week we've had," Iraola said.
Eddie Nketiah's stoppage-time penalty after a foul by Milos Kerkez was no consolation for Palace.
Palace manager Pierre Sage is in danger of being sacked after his side slumped to the bottom of the table following their seventh defeat in 10 league matches.
Brighton extended their superb start to the season, climbing to second place with a 2-0 win against Brentford at the Amex Stadium.
Diego Gomez put Brighton ahead early on before Brentford striker Igor Thiago was sent off.
Pascal Gross doubled Brighton's advantage with a 42nd minute penalty.
The Seagulls' sixth win in their last seven league games lifted them within five points of champions Arsenal, who beat Hull on Saturday.
Bournemouth striker Evanilson maintained his hot streak with a goal in a 2-1 win at Ipswich.

item.title: West Indies set Bangladesh 369 for victory in 2nd Test
item.description:
In its quest to level the two-match series against West Indies, Bangladesh got an improbable target of 369 to win the second and final Test at Sylhet International Cricket Stadium today.
Bangladesh had never won a Test, chasing more than 215 runs in their history in the fourth innings. However, Bangladesh won against the same opponent in 2009.
West Indies batted for one hour in the first hour of Day 5, leaving Bangladesh two and half sessions to bat for victory.
Resuming at 345-3, West Indies declared their second innings at 398-6. Kavem Hodge, the overnight unbeaten batter was able to add just two runs before being out for 142. Amir Jangoo who hit 133 in the first innings was not out on 39.
Bangladesh spinners then took some quick wickets, preventing West Indies from going on a berserk.
The three spinners-Taijul Islam, Nayeem Hasan and Mehidy Hasan Miraz-shared six wickets among them, with all of them taking two wickets each.
Earlier, West Indies were bowled out for 356 in the first innings, with Hasan Mahmud running through them with 6-90.
Towhid Hridoy then struck a monumental 242 not out, steering Bangladesh to 386, taking a 30-run lead.

item.title: Fire in China apartment building kills 14
item.description:
A fire that broke out in an apartment building in northern China killed at least 14 people, state media said Monday, raising the death toll from the previous night.
Deadly fires are relatively common in China due to lax building codes and an often slipshod approach to workplace safety.
The blaze occurred in a building in Shanxi province's Taiyuan city around 0900 GMT on Sunday, the official Xinhua news agency said that evening.
"A total of 38 people were sent to hospitals for treatment, among whom five have died," Xinhua reported, raising the death toll to 14 on Monday morning.
The flames were extinguished on Sunday, with search and rescue efforts completed, it said.
The cause of the fire is still under investigation.
China launched a campaign against fire hazards in high-rise buildings last November, after a huge blaze engulfed several tower blocks in Hong Kong, killing 168 people.
A month later, a fire at a residential building in southern China's Guangdong province killed 12 people.
And in July, a fire that engulfed a shoe factory in eastern China killed at least 28 people.

item.title: Trump vows comeback as bitter showdown with Congress looms
item.description:
Donald Trump vowed a political comeback Sunday as the major parties clashed over Democrat threats to prosecute top administration officials after the president's Republicans lost control of Congress in midterm elections.
The devastating results in last Tuesday's vote leave Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year "lame duck" period of his White House tenure. It also opens the door to multiple investigations by the Democrat-controlled Congress of the president, his family and senior members of his administration.
On political talk shows Sunday, incoming congressional leaders from the Democratic Party promised to hold Trump and his aides to account, while the president's top law officer resolved to defend them and Trump dug in his heels on social media.
"America took a giant step back in History with the results of the last Election," Trump said in a post on Truth Social, adding that the stock market that had grown during his tenure took a loss after the vote.
"But have no fear, we will be back, BIGGER AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE!"
On Friday, a defiant Trump appointed hardline advisor Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback -- even though many Republicans, including Vice President JD Vance, have reflected on why they had lost so badly at the ballot box.
Miller was architect of Trump's tough immigration policy, which analysts have identified as a contributing factor to the unpopularity of Republicans and their election debacle.
Amid Democrat threats for administration officials to "lawyer up," Trump said Saturday he was ordering the Justice Department to examine Democratic threats to impeach members of his administration, likening it to "extortion."
With control of committees in both chambers of Congress, Democrats can summon officials, demand documents and hold public hearings, putting Trump and his senior aides under intense scrutiny.
Likely subjects include the Trump family's business and cryptocurrency dealings, government contracts involving billionaire Elon Musk, cuts to federal agencies, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war.
Hakeem Jeffries, set to become speaker of the new Democrat-controlled House of Representatives, said he would support an effort to oust Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, a key architect of the war on Iran that began in February.
"I'm a hard yes on the Hegseth resolution," Jeffries told ABC, when asked about a Republican lawmaker's reported plan to introduce an impeachment motion as early as Monday.
"The so-called secretary of defense has abused his power, undermined our national security and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed prices on the American people and made the country less safe. Pete Hegseth has got to go."
Trump on Sunday defended Hegseth when talking with reporters, saying: "I mean he's guilty of two things, basically winning two wars," referring to the US raid on Venezuela in January that removed president Nicholas Maduro and the ongoing war with Iran.
"We won in Venezuela. We've taken out hundreds of billions of dollars. We won in 48 minutes. And we won in Iran," Trump told reporters. "It's just a question of closing it out now or later."
Attorney General Todd Blanche, a former personal lawyer for Trump and now head of the Justice Department, vowed to actively defend Trump and senior members of his administration.
"If they try to come after Stephen Miller...instead of actually just conducting oversight and leading, of course the Department of Justice will be there to defend him," Blanche told CNN.
Robert Garcia, the ranking Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, took aim at Blanche, saying one role of Congress under the US constitution is to hold the executive branch to account.
"All he wants to do is protect Donald Trump, is protect Donald Trump's cabinet and administration officials. That is not his job," Garcia told CNN, vowing to stop corruption and investigate "those that are committing crimes against the American public."
"They can come after us however they want. We're not going to be intimidated," added Garcia.

item.title: At least 35 killed in migrant boat sinking off Senegal
item.description:
A small boat carrying migrants sank off northwestern Senegal, killing at least 35 people in the latest tragedy along the dangerous Atlantic Ocean route from Africa to Europe, emergency services told AFP on Sunday.
Along this route, thousands of people have died in recent years trying to reach Spain's Canary Islands from west Africa.
An initial statement from the Senegalese interior ministry said 21 bodies and only one survivor had been recovered following the sinking, but that those numbers were provisional as the search continued.
Later Sunday, however, the Senegalese Press Agency (APS) said the toll now stood at 34 at least, a figure confirmed by Action for Human Rights and Friendship (ADHA) in a statement to AFP.
An "indeterminate number" of people were reported missing, APS added.
The toll then rose further on Sunday night to at least 35 with one survivor, according to the emergency services. "It's a provisional toll which has been changing since Friday."
An interior ministry source added: "The toll will unfortunately rise."
Media reports said the pirogue-type flat-bottom boat capsized on Saturday off the Loumpoul dunes in Kebemer department, between Dakar and the northern city of Saint-Louis.
However, Saliou Diouf, founder of Senegal's main migrant aid association Boza Fii, told AFP that the sinking occurred on Friday.
The nationalities of all the victims had not been confirmed as the search continues, he said.
"But the bodies recovered yesterday (Saturday) are Senegalese," he added.
Senegal's President Bassirou Diomaye Faye wrote on Facebook on Sunday: "All state authorities and resources have been mobilised to locate those who have gone missing, provide care for the survivors and support families."
Thousands of people from West Africa try each year to reach Europe on the perilous Atlantic route.
Senegalese authorities also said they had intercepted 142 migrants on Friday who were on a similar small boat aiming to reach Spain.
The group included 23 women, two babies and two other children, and were from Senegal, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea and Nigeria, according to police.
Senegal's interior ministry stressed "its determination to combat people smuggling networks, notably through strengthened cooperation with neighbouring countries" in a statement Sunday.
The country's interior minister would visit the region where the accident happened to meet families of the victims and express condolences on behalf of the state, it added.
Spanish authorities on the Canary Island of El Hierro declared an emergency on Saturday after a surge in migrant boat arrivals.
Since the start of November, El Hierro authorities said more than 3,300 people had arrived aboard around 30 boats.
Senegal, Mauritania and Morocco have stepped up maritime patrols around departure points for small boats, forcing them to head further south towards the coasts of Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, and Guinea, which prolongs the duration of the already hazardous crossing.

item.title: Minister: Sheikh Hasina will never return to Bangladesh
item.description:
Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Azam Khan on Sunday said Sheikh Hasina will never return to Bangladesh, warning that attempts to destabilise the country through sabotage will not be tolerated.
“We want Hasina to return to face trial and go to prison over the numerous allegations of genocide against her. But she will never return. Instead, she will spread rumours, destabilise the country and incite Awami League leaders and activists to engage in sabotage,” he said.
He made the remarks while speaking at a discussion meeting, organized by the Sakhipur upazila BNP on Sunday afternoon, marking the National Revolution and Solidarity Day.
The minister said Bangladesh had no room for sabotage and would move forward towards democracy and development.
He also criticised opposition parties for staging frequent demonstrations and issuing threats and ultimatums. While the prime minister was making efforts at home and abroad to tackle the fuel crisis, thousands of vehicles were being brought out in processions, wasting fuel, he said, calling the practice condemnable.
Ahmed Azam Khan urged the government to be given five years to govern, saying the next election would be held after that period under a system ensuring people's voting rights.
“There will be no election under a partisan government. Voting will take place during the day, not at night, and no one will be allowed to cast another person's vote,” he said. Urging opposition parties to exercise restraint, he warned that people would reject those whose actions disrupted development and created instability.

item.title: Crude bomb thrown into Pallabi police station from flyover
item.description:
A crude bomb was thrown into the compound of Pallabi police station from an adjacent flyover in Dhaka on Sunday night.
The incident occurred at around 8:15pm.
The perpetrators have yet to be identified.
Pallabi police station Duty Officer Ibrahim Khalil said senior police officials were looking into the incident.
CCTV footage from nearby cameras would be examined to identify those responsible, he added.
Earlier in the day, four separate crude bomb explosions were reported at different locations on the Dhaka University campus around 6:30pm.

item.title: Four crude bomb explosions reported at DU, two held
item.description:
Crude bomb explosions were reported at four locations on the Dhaka University (DU) campus on Sunday evening, while students detained two people allegedly attempting to set off another bomb near the Teacher-Student Centre (TSC).
The incidents took place around 6:30pm. Students later handed the two detainees over to the university’s proctorial team.
According to preliminary information, explosions occurred beside the university’s administrative building, at VC Chattar, in front of the Mukti O Gonotontro Toron near Nilkhet, and in the TSC area.
At the TSC, students detained two people while they were allegedly attempting to set off a cocktail. The device may have been thrown towards the area from the direction of Suhrawardy Udyan, according to initial reports.
DU Proctor Professor Mohammad Israfil Prang said students detained the two individuals following the incident near the TSC and handed them over to the proctorial team.
“They are being taken to the proctor’s office. We have already informed Shahbagh police. We are reviewing CCTV footage to understand what happened,” he said.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,282 as two die in 24hrs
item.description:
Two children died with measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours ending at 8:00am on Sunday, bringing the country’s combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 1,282 this year.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified the latest fatalities as suspected measles deaths.
With these, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,177, while confirmed deaths from measles have remained the same at 105.
A total of 1,138 new suspected measles cases were reported during the 24-hour period, pushing the cumulative number of suspected cases nationwide to 238,840.
Meanwhile, 87 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 24,442.
Since March 15 this year, a total of 212,979 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 204,049 have recovered, according to DGHS data.

item.title: Shama: Rohingya crisis now a security concern for Bangladesh
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Sunday said the Rohingya crisis has become a security concern for Bangladesh, stressing the need to keep the issue high on the international agenda.
"We need to keep the Rohingya issue relevant on the international stage, and keeping it relevant remains a major challenge," she said while speaking as the chief guest at a dialogue.
Neeti Gobeshona Kendro organized the national policy dialogue titled "A Sustainable Approach to the Resolution of the Rohingya Crisis: Outline of a National Strategy and External Contribution" at the CIRDAP Auditorium.
The state minister said Bangladesh must press the international community to engage meaningfully with Myanmar to ensure that the necessary conditions are created inside the country for the safe and dignified return of the Rohingyas.
She also underscored the importance of building a national political consensus on addressing the crisis.
"We have always been vocal about the Rohingya crisis," Shama Obaed said emphasizing that repatriation must take place in a safe and dignified manner.
"We need to ensure minimum dignity for them," she said.
Bangladesh is currently hosting more than 1.3 million Rohingyas, with the number continuing to grow, putting increasing pressure on host communities and the country's economy as a whole.
The dialogue aimed to facilitate constructive engagement among policymakers, political leaders, diplomats, researchers, civil society representatives, human rights advocates, journalists and representatives of the Rohingya community on developing a sustainable and comprehensive approach to resolving the protracted crisis.
Particular emphasis was placed on formulating a national strategic framework, building political consensus, strengthening diplomatic engagement and exploring the roles of international and external stakeholders.
The discussion highlighted the importance of sustained policy dialogue, diplomatic engagement, political consensus and meaningful participation of the Rohingya community in finding a durable and dignified solution to one of the most protracted humanitarian and geopolitical challenges facing Bangladesh and the wider region.

item.title: Minister: Hasina is a convict, legal steps taken to bring her back
item.description:
Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Md Asaduzzaman on Sunday said the government is following due legal procedures to bring ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina back to Bangladesh, describing her as a convicted criminal.
“To me, she is a criminal. She is a convict, sentenced by our tribunal. That is her identity to us. Legal procedures are underway to bring her back,” he said.
The minister made the remarks after inaugurating a workshop on "Integrity in Judicial Proceedings" organized by Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) at a hotel in Dhaka.
“Whatever needs to be done legally concerning Sheikh Hasina, we are doing that through due process. You will see how we deal with it legally when we take any steps. There is no room for emotion here. The matter is that I will enforce the law. If we fail to enforce the law properly, then you can question us,” he said.
Asked whether the government would fight a legal battle in an Indian court to bring her back, the minister said it is a matter for the Indian government.
“We have sent a request to them under the extradition treaty. If they hand her over to us, we will bring her under the law through due process in the manner required,” he said.
When a journalist questioned the extradition treaty, saying Hasina was staying in India as a state guest rather than being held as a prisoner, Asaduzzaman said her status as described by Indian authorities did not change Bangladesh’s position.
“They may say whatever they want, but that is not enough. She was tried in an open court in my country. Since you are raising this question, first consider whether 1,400 people were killed during the July Revolution and whether 30,000 people were left disabled,” he said.
He also questioned whether the trial had any shortcomings, whether it was held behind closed doors and whether witnesses had been allowed to testify.
“We have sent the request that is required under due process to bring her back. That is what I am saying,” the minister added.

item.title: Kali Puja festivities set to begin across Bangladesh
item.description:
The Hindu communities across Bangladesh are celebrating Kali Puja, also known as Shyama Puja, on Sunday night with religious rituals, traditional festivities and prayers dedicated to Goddess Kali.
Temples and households are ready to welcome the auspicious occasion with special worship of Goddess Kali, illumination with earthen lamps and candles, devotional music and various religious rituals.
Kali Puja, popularly known as Deepabali or the festival of lights, is observed on the new moon night (Amavasya) of the Bengali month of Kartik. The festival is dedicated to Goddess Kali, regarded as the embodiment of divine power, strength, wisdom and the destruction of evil.
As part of the celebration, devotees will illuminate their homes, temples and crematoriums with earthen lamps (pradeep) and candles in remembrance of their ancestors.
In the capital, elaborate preparations have been made to celebrate the festival at Dhakeshwari National Temple, Ramkrishna Math and Mission, Siddheshwari Kali Mandir, Ramna Kali Mandir, Sri Sri Baradeshwari Kalimata Temple, Radha Gobinda Jeo Temple, Postogola Crematorium, Biharilal Jeo Temple in Sutrapur, Gautam Mandir, Ramseeta Mandir, Shibmandir in Shankharibazar, Tanti Bazar and Bangla Bazar.
According to the puja schedule, worship of Goddess Kali will begin at midnight at different temples, followed by the offering of anjali, “hom-joggo” and distribution of mahaprasad among the devotees.
According to Hindu mythology, Goddess Kali is a fierce manifestation of Goddess Durga, who emerged to fight the forces of evil. Legend has it that after a fierce battle with demonic forces, Kali became so consumed by her destructive rage that Lord Shiva had to lie beneath her feet to stop her.
Realizing that she had stepped on her consort, she stuck out her tongue in astonishment and brought her rampage to an end.
The key message of Kali Puja is the triumph of good over evil and the destruction of negative forces both in the external world and within human beings.
The largest celebrations in the capital traditionally take place in Shakhari Bazar and Tanti Bazarin Old Dhaka.
A festive atmosphere has already emerged in the two neighbourhoods, where makeshift pandals have been erected and temples decorated with colorful lights and ornamental designs.
Meanwhile, business activities related to the festival are gaining momentum in the old part of the capital, with devotees and families flocking to markets to purchase puja essentials, including candles, earthen lamps (pradeep) and other ritual items.

item.title: 33 BGB platoons deployed across Dhaka, Gazipur, Narayanganj
item.description:
A total of 33 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) have been deployed across industrial areas in Dhaka, Gazipur and Narayanganj amid ongoing workers' unrest.
The deployment aims to maintain law and order, strengthen security in industrial zones and prevent further incidents, the BGB said in a statement issued on Sunday morning.
In Dhaka, BGB personnel are deployed in Savar, Ashulia and Mirpur.
In Narayanganj, they are overseeing security in Shibu Market, Jalkuri, the BSCIC Industrial Estate, Chashara, Kanchpur and Shimrail.
In Gazipur, the deployment covers Chandra, Palli Bidyut, Mouchak, Ambag, Kashimpur, Naojor, Bhogra Bypass, Gacha and Salna.
The BGB headquarters' monitoring cell is also monitoring field operations and live footage through technology-based systems, according to the statement.
Deployed personnel remain on high alert and are working in coordination with local administrations and police.
The BGB said deployment and surveillance operations would continue to maintain a safe and stable working environment in industrial areas, protect lives and property, and ensure public security.

item.title: Bus torched in Savar after three consecutive nights of fires in Dhamrai
item.description:
Two more buses were set on fire in separate incidents in Savar and Dhamrai early Sunday, taking the total number of buses torched in the two upazilas to four in four nights. No casualties were reported.
Jahangir Alam, senior station officer of Savar Fire Service, and Al-Amin Khan, station officer of Dhamrai Fire Station, confirmed the incidents on Sunday morning.
The fires broke out near the Savar Thana Bus Stand and in the Sharifbag area of Dhamrai, both along the Dhaka-Aricha Highway.
According to Savar Fire Service, it received a report of a fire involving a Savar Paribahan bus parked near the Savar Thana Bus Stand at 2:55am.
Two fire service units rushed to the scene and brought the blaze under control by 3:10am.
Jahangir Alam said preliminary findings suggested that the bus had been set on fire. He estimated the damage at around Tk2 lakh.
Meanwhile, a D-Link Paribahan bus caught fire in front of Afaz Uddin College in Dhamrai’s Sharifbag area around 3:40am, according to the Dhamrai Fire Service.
Two units responded to the incident and extinguished the fire by 4:20am.
Al-Amin Khan said the bus was mainly used to transport employees of Snotex Garments to and from Nabinagar. It was parked when the fire broke out.
He said preliminary findings suggested that the bus had been deliberately set on fire.
The latest incident marks the third consecutive night of bus fires in Dhamrai. On Thursday night, November 5, a bus belonging to Pavel Paribahan, which was undergoing repairs, caught fire on Dhamrai Thana Road.
The following night, a Polli Seba Paribahan bus was set on fire in the Srirampur area along the Dhaka-Aricha Highway.
Dhamrai police station Officer-in-Charge Md Nazmul Huda Khan said three buses had been set on fire in the upazila over three consecutive nights.
He said police had advised bus owners after the previous incident to keep their vehicles in secure locations, under guard or close surveillance.
“Despite this, another bus left outside was set on fire. We are investigating whether these incidents are politically motivated, stem from personal disputes or are related to other factors,” he said.
The OC said the owner of one of the affected buses had filed a complaint with the police station. Police were treating the incidents seriously and working to establish the circumstances behind them.

item.title: Brahmanbaria road, rail blockade lifted after 4hrs; protesters issue 72hrs ultimatum
item.description:
Residents lifted a four-hour blockade of roads and railway lines in Brahmanbaria on Sunday after receiving assurances from a local BNP leader over their demands to restore six villages to Basudeb Union and oppose the proposed formation of a new upazila.
The protesters called off the blockade around 11am after Sirajul Islam Siraj, general secretary of the district BNP and administrator of the district council, arrived at the scene and assured them that their demands would be addressed.
However, they warned that they would resume the blockade if their demands were not met within 72 hours.
The demonstration began at 7am in the Kodda area of Brahmanbaria Sadar Upazila, where residents blocked the Dhaka-Agartala highway and the Dhaka-Chittagong and Dhaka-Sylhet railway lines.
The blockade brought road traffic to a standstill in both directions and left at least seven intercity trains stranded at different stations, causing hardship for thousands of passengers.
Jahangir Alam Bhuiyan Nayan, president of Basudeb Union BNP, said several villages had recently been separated from Basudeb Union to form a new union named Barisal.
He alleged that residents of the affected villages, including Basudeb, Kodda, Chandi and Korabaria, were not consulted before the decision was made.
He also alleged that the new union was formed under the influence of district BNP leader Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan, whose father, Fazlur Rahman Bhuiyan, was appointed its administrator.
According to Jahangir, there are also plans to form a new upazila, also named Barishal, comprising several unions from Brahmanbaria Sadar and Bijoynagar upazilas.
The protesters are demanding that the separated villages be brought back under Basudeb Union and opposing the proposed upazila.
Dulal Mia, a resident of Chandi village, alleged that Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan was driving the initiatives by using the influence of his brother, Abdur Rahman Sunny, who serves as assistant private secretary-2 to the prime minister.
No comments could be obtained from the individuals named in the allegations.
Sirajul Islam Siraj arrived at the protest site around 10:30am. Following his assurances, the protesters withdrew the blockade at around 11am, allowing road and rail services to resume.
The protesters reiterated that they would block both roads and railway lines again if their demands were not met within 72 hours.
